#2640. The NFL officials who pulled double duty got double pay (as they should)

Some things go without saying. Nowadays, however, it’s sometimes important to state the obvious.

Via Mark Maske of Front Office Sports, the four officials who ended up officiating two games on Sunday (Don Willard, Terry Killens, Jabir Walker, and Justin Larrew) will get paid for working two games.

Why wouldn’t they? Getting twice the pay for twice the work should be a given. The real question is whether they should have gotten even more.

Folks who work overtime usually get time-and-a-half pay. In some instances, going above and beyond the call of duty results in double pay.

Here’s the real question — did the officials who were supposed to work one game in Week 10 but didn’t get still get their pay? Or do officials only get paid for the games they actually officiate, even if/when the NFL seemingly overreacts, reshuffles the deck, and cancels an official’s assignment that the official was otherwise ready and willing to fulfill?

It still seems that the NFL overreacted to the situation, turning the officiating assignments upside down in lieu of deciding to do whatever needed to be done to get the officials to their assigned game so that the existing crews wouldn’t be disrupted.

#2633. NBA trade rumors 2026-27: Dejounte Murray market lukewarm, what about Zion Williamson?

NBA front offices generally wait about 20 games to assess their teams before seriously looking into the trade market. Even more, it's not until Dec. 15, when many contracts signed over the summer become trade-eligible, that the market really heats up. That, however, never stops the NBA trade rumor mill, so here is the latest.

Soon after news broke of Dejounte Murray's agent requesting a trade for the point guard out of New Orleans, rumors tried to link Murray to the Phoenix Suns. There was some logic to it: The salaries line up and, at least outside the Valley of the Sun, the sense is Phoenix could use a point guard.

However, most of that speculation seemed to come out of Murray's camp, not Phoenix, which has limited interest in him, according to multiple reports, including Chris Manix here at NBC Sports. He also reports the market for Murray is "lukewarm." Actually, lukewarm may be putting it kindly. Here is what one "high ranking" NBA executive told Kelly Iko of Yahoo Sports:

"What a f****** mess. No one wants to touch him."

Coming off a torn Achilles that cost him most of two seasons, other teams see Murray as a distressed asset making $32.8 million this season, with a player option he almost certainly picks up for $30.8 million next season. Teams will want picks, likely a first-round pick, to take on that much money. Based on the history of Pelicans lead executive Joe Dumars in dealing with Trey Murphy III and Herb Jones (two players other teams actually want), this is going to drag out.

The Sacramento Kings are 1-12 and their coach, Doug Christie, is in the final year of his contract. On 29 teams in the league, that would be the definition of a coach on the hot seat, but in Sacramento they pushed back hard when the idea first came out, saying Christie was safe. He is a favorite of ownership there.

That hasn't completely changed. Marc Stein of The Stein Line reports the Kings "would prefer not to fire" Christie during the season to limit the amount of "tumult and upheaval" during Darius Acuff Jr.'s rookie campaign. Most likely, Christie is let go after the season. If/when that happens, two names to watch are Tom Thibodeau and Mark Jackson. Thibodeau (who has connections to GM Scott Perry) has coached more recently and had more success, while former Warriors coach Mark Jackson is a favorite of owner Vivek Ranadive from those days in Golden State.

In other Sacramento news, they are still interested in adding veteran point guard Gabe Vincent as a backup behind Acuff, he has a standing offer, Stein reports. That he hasn't jumped at the deal could be telling.

• With all the Pelicans trade talk right now, would they consider trading Zion Williamson? Maybe, but the return isn't going to be as robust as they might hope, reports ESPN's Tim MacMahon on the Hoop Collective podcast: "He's somewhere on the LaMelo (Ball) to Ja (Morant) spectrum, in terms of trade value." Ball went for a first-round pick and Naz Reid, plus three pick swaps, and MacMahon is saying Williamson would get a smaller return than that. Morant was traded for Jerami Grant and Kris Murray.

• While the Miami Heat have found a groove of late, this is a team known to be looking for upgrades, and Ira Winderman of the Sun Sentinel suggests to watch out for Zach LaVine as a target.

• The Indiana Pacers may be in the market to trade for a wing, but they want to get Tyrese Haliburton back healthy and let things shake out first, Stein reports.

#2630. Red Sox Sign Michael Arias To Minor League Deal

The Boston Red Sox have agreed to a minor league contract with reliever Michael Arias, according to Andrew Parker of Sox Prospects. The right-handed pitcher will attend spring training as a non-roster invitee, meaning he must fight for a spot on the final roster or face assignment to Triple-A Worcester. In Double-A, Arias pitched for the Yankees during the 2026 season, recording a 5.20 earned run average over 53 2/3 innings, according to MLB Trade Rumors. His performance last year included striking out 24% of opponents while allowing a 10% walk rate, a mix that shows promise but also highlights the control issues that have plagued his career.

Arias has been a journeyman in the minor leagues, bouncing between organizations since he turned his focus to pitching in 2021 after playing shortstop. He reached Triple-A with the Cubs in 2024, but his time in the New York farm system was spent mostly at the High-A and Double-A levels. Although the Yankees included him on their 40-man roster for the entire previous year, they chose to non-tender him when the season concluded.

Despite the Yankees immediately bringing him back on a minor league deal, he never moved above Double-A due to his pedestrian performance. Arias receives a non-roster invite now, but he is a long shot to break camp with Boston. With an eye on a midseason MLB debut, he is targeting a season-starting assignment with Triple-A Worcester. For a converted shortstop who has been pitching for only five years and has struggled to throw enough strikes throughout his minor league career, this path is familiar.

The numbers from last season show a pitcher who has raw stuff but still struggles with command. His walk rate was still a little high last year, though it marked his lowest full-season mark. His recent performance in the Dominican Winter League offers some hope, as he has issued only three free passes across 10 2/3 innings so far. This improvement in control could be the difference between a long shot and a viable bullpen option for the Red Sox. Teams need pitchers who can get hitters out without walking them, and Arias is trying to prove he can do both.

Boston is looking for depth in their relief corps, and a player with Arias's background offers a low-risk opportunity. Although his raw stuff garnered some prospect attention, the consistency has been missing. If he can lower his walk rate further, he might earn a spot in the big league club. The Red Sox are taking a chance on a player who has been on multiple 40-man rosters but has yet to stick in the majors.

#2628. ESPN chief: Media coverage of Joe Buck, Troy Aikman dustup is "disappointing"

The Joe Buck vs. Troy Aikman Real Broadcasters of the NFL drama has added another layer of unexpected reality to the ultimate reality show that is pro football. Their mutual boss claims that ESPN doesn’t like the coverage of the situation.

“Joe and Troy have done a great job for us on Monday Night Football.” ESPN president Jimmy Pitaro said Tuesday at the SBJ Media Innovators conference, via Brandon Contes of Awful Announcing. “When I say ‘us,’ they’ve done a great job for ESPN, they’ve done a great job for the league, they’ve done a great job for the game, and most importantly, they’ve done a great job for fans.

“Are we happy about the media coverage recently? Of course not. It’s been disappointing. But these guys are professionals, and they’re delivering every week. If you watched it last night, another super high-quality production and telecast, and I’d fully expect that to continue that through the season and through the Super Bowl.”

At some level, they shouldn’t be disappointed. Any attention is, at some level, good attention. While it’s unlikely that anyone is tuning in for a Monday night game solely to witness the interactions of Buck and Aikman, it adds a little extra something to the overall buzz arising from the broadcast.

The deeper question is who Pitaro and the other big shots at ESPN are “disappointed” with. The situation didn’t come to light because everyone involved decided to keep the dirty laundry in house. People started talking privately. Aikman has said plenty publicly that confirms the situation and otherwise stirs the pot.

ESPN has no cause to be disappointed with those who did their jobs by pulling the threads of a genuinely interesting, uncontived, and in many ways unprecedented story. If the folks who write the checks should be miffed at anyone, it should be at the recipients of those checks who decided not to hold their own tongues in check regarding an obviously sensitive situation.

#2625. Jacoby Brissett report card: Grading his first start with the Ravens

Give him credit. Jacoby Brissett gave the Baltimore Ravens something they desperately needed: a productive passing game. Making his first start for the team with the running game ineffective, the veteran was needed to carry the team, and he did for stretches.

Brissett attempted 49 passes. He completed 33 and threw for 340 yards against a Los Angeles Chargers team that honestly controlled this game. Baltimore's fourth starting quarterback of the season delivered an encouraging performance, especially considering how little time he had to get comfortable with his new teammates and offensive system.

The volume deserves consideration alongside the yardage. Brissett averaged 6.9 yards per attempt and finished without a touchdown pass, so the 340-yard total reflects both productive stretches and how heavily Baltimore relied on him. His debut improved the Ravens' ability to move the ball, but it did not eliminate stalled possessions or turnover opportunities.

Brissett wasn't perfect, and his interception proved costly. However, he made several important throws. He kept Baltimore within striking distance and gave the offense a chance to compete despite an almost nonexistent rushing attack.

Derrick Henry scored twice, but the Ravens managed just 16 rushing yards as a team. Unfortunately, individual progress doesn't show up in the standings. Baltimore lost 23-20, extending its losing streak to five games. Brissett deserved a better result for his first start, but the Ravens' familiar problems once again overshadowed a promising performance.

It took a while for Brissett to settle in, but he eventually started connecting on some important throws. During Baltimore's fourth offensive drive, on third-and-10 from the Ravens' 35-yard line, he found Mark Andrews right on the numbers for a 10-yard completion and a first down.

It was a well-placed pass in a situation where the offense desperately needed to keep the drive alive. Two plays later, Brissett delivered another quality throw, finding Zay Flowers for 17 yards on second-and-nine to move the chains again. He followed that with a 24-yard completion on second-and-15 from the Chargers' 26-yard line, setting up a goal-to-go scenario and Henry's first touchdown of the evening.

Brissett also showed he could push the ball downfield when the situation called for it. With fewer than two minutes remaining in the first half, he connected with Ja'Kobi Lane for a 31-yard gain to get Baltimore's two-minute drill moving; with just over two minutes remaining in the fourth quarter, he escaped pressure and a near sack before finding Andrews near the right sideline for another first down. That play demonstrated the veteran's ability to remain composed when the pocket breaks down.

Brissett's productive stretch on Baltimore's fourth possession came with a little good fortune. One play before his third-down completion to Andrews, a pass that should have been intercepted fell incomplete. The Chargers had a chance to get the ball but couldn't finish the play. Brissett made them pay by converting the next opportunity.

His first interception as a Raven came on Baltimore's fifth possession. The pass was deflected, allowing the Chargers to come away with a promising drive. There was also a reasonable argument that Lane was interfered with on the play, but the result stood. Regardless of the circumstances, the turnover allowed Los Angeles to regain control of the game.

The interception was a blemish on an otherwise productive night, particularly because Baltimore couldn't afford to surrender possessions. Brissett finished with one interception, while the Ravens committed two turnovers overall. The other came on Flowers' late fumble, which effectively ended Baltimore's comeback attempt.

Brissett completed 33 of 49 passes, good for a 67.3% completion rate, and finished with 340 yards. He consistently found receivers when Baltimore needed to move the chains, including several key completions to Andrews and Flowers. His ball placement on those throws helped keep drives alive. There was room for improvement, but the overall accuracy was encouraging.

Brissett did a good job distributing the football and finding opportunities in the passing game. Andrews finished with eight receptions on eight targets for 82 yards, while Flowers and Lane also made meaningful contributions. Brissett wasn't limited to one target, and his ability to work the ball around helped Baltimore generate offense despite its struggles on the ground.

This was arguably Brissett's strongest category. He showed composure when pressure arrived, most notably on the fourth-quarter completion to Andrews after escaping a near sack. His 31-yard connection with Lane also demonstrated confidence in pushing the ball downfield when Baltimore needed a spark. Brissett didn't allow the circumstances of his first start to overwhelm him.

At least two tosses should have been intercepted but weren't, and even though Brissett drops, that keeps this grade from being higher. The deflected interception gave the Chargers a valuable possession. In the end, he was only intercepted once, but he put the ball in harm's way, and that deserves consideration.

Brissett had a difficult assignment, stepping into a new offense and trying to stabilize a team that had lost four straight games. He gave Baltimore a chance to compete and continued making plays even as the rushing attack struggled to provide support. His response to pressure and ability to keep the offense moving were encouraging signs for a quarterback still learning his surroundings.

Brissett deserved better than a loss in his first start with Baltimore. He threw for 340 yards, completed more than two-thirds of his attempts and gave the Ravens a passing attack that had been missing during their recent struggles. His interception was costly, but it shouldn't overshadow the positives. One has to wonder if the Ravens might have won more if he had arrived earlier.

Brissett earned a B because he gave Baltimore functional quarterback play under difficult circumstances while leaving several decisions open to criticism. His completions to Andrews and ability to extend plays offered reasons for encouragement, but the dangerous throws prevent this from being graded solely on yardage and completion percentage.

The next step is greater efficiency within an offense that provides more support. Baltimore cannot expect its newest quarterback to sustain a weekly workload approaching 50 attempts while the running game contributes almost nothing. Brissett showed he can help; the Ravens still need to build a more dependable offense around him.

This article originally appeared on Ravens Wire: Jacoby Brissett report card: Grading his first start with the Ravens

#2619. Dan Campbell won't wallow in "what ifs" arising from injuries

The Lions have, in recent weeks, lost both linebacker Jack Campbell (neck) and defensive end Aidan Hutchinson (knee) to significant injuries. Coach Dan Campbell won’t wallow in worrying about what may have been if the injuries hadn’t occurred.

“I think there’s times where, if you’re not careful, you lay in bed at night and you start thinking about all the ‘what ifs,’” Campbell told reporters on Tuesday. “And at some point, you just become a miserable piece of shit. And I’m not gonna do it, man. We’re not doing it.

“I refuse to look at it that way. Does it sting? Yeah, it sure did in the moment. It’s time to move on. We have to.

“And what has happened with Jack Campbell and with Hutch now will not be in vain. We can’t allow it to. They got us to this point. And so what are we gonna do about it, man? Are we just gonna let it go to waste, or are we gonna do something and pick up the slack?”

It’s the right attitude. Injuries happen. Sometimes, they happen to great players. (The more great players a team has, the greater the chances that one of them will be injured.)

The only approach is to tap the next man up on the shoulder, expect him to do his job to the best of his ability, not allow it to become a “woe is us” situation, and keep going.

That becomes easier, of course, if a team has quality depth. Which is why some teams that are top heavy with highly-paid stars find themselves in a pinch when those stars aren’t available to play.

Ramona Shelburne gave her honest thoughts on the Lakers this season.

Luka Doncic (77) and Austin Reaves (15) of the Los Angeles Lakers look on during a game against the Toronto Raptors on Sunday, Nov. 1, 2026, in Los Angeles. NBAE via Getty Images

While Los Angeles' 12-2 record hasn't come by defeating all the NBA's best teams, the Lakers' early strength of schedule ranks around 14th to 16th. That means the cumulative strength of schedule is around league average, not one of the easiest as Shelburne implied.

NBA on ESPN's post of Shelburne's take was not received well by many as a Community Note was added, stating: "Analyses rank the Lakers' played schedule near average or slightly easier than league average in strength, not one of the easiest; Spurs and Memphis rank easier per opponent records and models."

Shelburne chose to defend her take the following day and went on an unfiltered rant on ESPN's radio show Tuesday morning.

Shelburne remains a brilliant writer and respected NBA insider, but her reporting on the Lakers, at times, lights a fire under fans.

#2609. Indiana Fever GM search narrows, multiple candidates come with NBA ties: Sources

The Indiana Fever's search for a new general manager is ramping up.

The franchise is expected to evaluate several finalists, including many with NBA backgrounds, and make a hire in the next few weeks, according to multiple sources familiar with the search who were granted anonymity because they are not permitted to speak publicly about the search process.

Among the list of candidates being considered are Sacramento Kings vice president of basketball operations and player personnel Phil Jabour, Boston Celtics vice president of team operations and organizational growth Allison Feaster and former Dallas Mavericks assistant general manager Matt Ricardi. Clare Duwelius, former Minnesota Lynx basketball operations manager and current Unrivaled general manager and executive vice president, was also being considered at one point in the search process.

The Fever's front office overhaul began on Oct. 23 when the franchise announced longtime president Kelly Krauskopf would step down after three decades with Pacers Sports & Entertainment. She informed leadership of her decision before the end of the 2026 season. Later that same day news broke that the Fever had fired general manager Amber Cox after two seasons.

Cox's firing followed her heavily scrutinized exit interview, during which she was dismissive of critiques of the Fever fan base. Four-time All-Star Kelsey Mitchell shared comments during the same session that directly contradicted Cox, detailing difficulties of competing for fans who she said "that may not like you." She added that the organization is "unbelievable," but said it hasn't been easy "trying to be yourself."

Fever coach Stephanie White has one year left on her contract and is expected to remain in her position, according to a source familiar with discussions who spoke on the condition of anonymity to preserve relationships. White represented the Fever at last week's WNBA competition committee meeting, which includes league leadership along with coaches and general managers from every team.

The Fever shakeup was the first step in what is expected to be one of the most critical free agency periods in the franchise's history that starts with an attempt to re-sign Mitchell who is an unrestricted free agent. The Fever also will look to extend three-time All-Star Caitlin Clark under the league's new EPIC (Exceptional Performance on Initial Contract) clause. A highly anticipated lever in the league's new collective bargaining agreement, the EPIC clause allows players signed to their rookie scale contract who have been named MVP or to an All-WNBA first or second team to renegotiate the final year of their rookie contract to sign a multi-year extension.

Four-time All-Star Aliyah Boston signed an extension under the EPIC provision in April, keeping her with the franchise through 2029. Despite boasting the top offense in the league, powered by record breaking seasons from Mitchell and Clark, the Fever were bounced by the Las Vegas Aces in the first round of the playoffs. The Fever have failed to make it past the semifinals since drafting Clark with the No. 1 overall pick in 2024.

Pacers Sports & Entertainment hired Excel Search & Advisory to lead the search for a new Fever general manager. The firm is also leading the league's search for a new commissioner. Clark is represented by the agency's sports management sector.

Riccardi, who worked in the Brooklyn Nets organization in a variety of roles from 2010 to 2022, was with the Dallas Mavericks from 2022 to 2026. He spent most of his last year there as the interim co-general manager, and had been elevated from his assistant general manager position when former president of basketball operations Nico Harrison was fired from his post. Riccardi was a finalist to replace Harrison, but the job ultimately went to Masai Ujiri.

Feaster, a Harvard graduate and three-time Ivy League Player of the Year, was drafted fifth overall by the Los Angeles Sparks in 1998 and finished her WNBA career with the Fever in 2008. (She played overseas until retiring in 2016.) She joined the Celtics as their director of player development in September 2019 and was later promoted to vice president of player development and organizational growth.

Jabour, who has been with the Sacramento Kings since October 2020, is their vice president of basketball operations and player personnel. He has spent two decades in the NBA, previously with Houston, Orlando and Philadelphia in a variety of roles.

The Fever are one of nine WNBA franchises with varying levels of shared ownership with an NBA franchise. Conversations around both leagues about their GM search have included an expectation that the Fever will operate more closely in line with their NBA counterpart. That is already being reflected in the franchise's $78 million investment into a state-of-the-art practice facility which is scheduled to open this coming spring, but also in their comprehensive team staffing.

#2607. Sources: Closer David Bednar accepts record-setting qualifying offer from Yankees

NEW YORK — David Bednar accepted the qualifying offer from the Yankees ahead of Tuesday's 4 p.m. deadline, multiple sources confirmed to the New York Daily News.

The one-year, $23.15 million deal gives Bednar a record average annual salary for a reliever, topping the $23 million that Edwin Díaz got from the Dodgers on a three-year deal last winter. Still, it is somewhat surprising that Bednar didn't reject the qualifying offer and pursue a larger total sum on a multi-year contract in a market short on established closers, even if doing so would have attached international bonus pool money and draft pick compensation to his free agency.

Of course, Bednar and the Yankees can still work out a longer deal down the road. Regardless, the Yanks can rest easy knowing that they've locked in their closer for 2027, achieving an offseason goal.

"Hopefully, we find a way to keep him," Brian Cashman said of Bednar at the GM Meetings last week.

Bednar, 32, owns a 2.85 ERA since 2021 despite a disastrous 2024 campaign in Pittsburgh. The righty has thrived with the Yankees since being acquired from the Pirates ahead of the 2025 trade deadline, recording a 2.39 ERA and 45 saves over 94 innings. That includes 35 saves in 39 opportunities and a 2.47 ERA this past season.

Bednar, a two-time All-Star, also ranked in the 88th percentile or better in xERA, Chase%, Whiff%, Barrel% and ground-ball rate in 2026, and he has a 1.00 ERA over nine postseason innings for the Yankees. He's shown that the bright lights of the Bronx do not bother him, which played a part in the Yankees extending the qualifying offer.

"We dropped a big qualifying number on him," Cashman said. "That factored a lot. He's a cool customer."

Cashman also noted that Bednar has become a leader in the Bombers' bullpen.

With Bednar accepting a $23.15 million salary for 2027, the Yankees are committing big money to a free agent reliever for the first time since Zack Britton ($39 million) and Adam Ottavino ($27 million) signed three-year contracts in January 2019. While Aroldis Chapman also signed a hefty extension with the team in November 2019, the Yankees' biggest multi-year contracts for free agent relievers have gone to Justin Wilson (2 years, $5.5 million) and Tommy Kahnle (2 years, $11.5 million) since then.

They also haven't paid a reliever a single-season salary higher than the $9 million Bednar made in 2026 since Chapman, Britton and Ottavino's contracts soured.

But with the Yankees' bullpen in need of a makeover this offseason — they didn't have any obvious incumbents to replace Bednar in the closer's role — Cashman said that he's "not afraid" to spend lavishly on multiple relievers.

Cashman also called the reconstruction of his bullpen an offseason "priority." That's because a lot of spots are vacant.

While the Yankees have already agreed on a cheap deal to bring Tim Hill back for depth, the team has four other free agent relievers in Paul Blackburn, Ryan Yarbrough, John Schreiber and Michael Fulmer. That makes Brent Headrick the only other contracted reliever without health concerns who spent the entire 2026 season on the Yankees' roster. Other relievers on the 40-man roster include Fernando Cruz, Kervin Castro, Angel Chivilli, Yerry De los Santos, Bradley Hanner and Luis Gil. Cruz is coming off a partially torn UCL and could be a non-tender candidate. The rest are far from solidified big leaguers.

In addition to Bednar, the Yankees would love to re-sign Blackburn after a career year, and they've checked in on Yarbrough, another depth piece.

As for external free-agent options, Adrian Morejon is another big-ticket arm who got the qualifying offer but rejected it. He garnered interest from the Yankees at the trade deadline, but it remains to be seen if they are truly "not afraid" to swim in the lefty's pricey waters after Bednar's acceptance of the qualifying offer.

Alex Vesia and JoJo Romero are intriguing options as well.

Bednar was one of two players to accept the qualifying offer on Tuesday. The other was Twins catcher Ryan Jeffers, a player the Yankees had interest in ahead of the trade deadline this past summer. He's not longer an option with Cashman looking for a right-handed hitting backstop to pair with Austin Wells.

Bednar is the second Yankee to accept the qualifying offer in as many offseasons. Last year, Trent Grisham took the one-year pact when it was valued at $22.05 million. The Yankees are hoping their investment in Bednar yields better results, as Grisham is back on the open market after an injury-riddled year that saw him regress offensively and defensively.

#2606. NFL news, live updates: Aidan Hutchinson reportedly suffers torn ACL on sack celebration; Patriots QB Drake Maye out indefinitely with ankle injury

Another NFL Sunday is in the books, with just one game left in Week 10 as the Baltimore Ravens host the LA Chargers on "Monday Night Football."

Sunday kicked off with a bang as the Detroit Lions and New England Patriots faced off in Munich, Germany, with injuries to two stars that will have all eyes drawn as the new week plays out. Lions star defensive end Aidan Hutchinson suffered what is feared to be a season-ending ACL tear while celebrating a sack against Patriots quarterback Drake Maye … who suffered an ankle injury on that very sack, which knocked him out of the game and could cost him the season.

Week 10 also offered us our first look at Las Vegas Raiders No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza as a starter. He led scoring drives on each of the Raiders' first two possessions and entered halftime with a 10-7 lead over the Seattle Seahawks, but Drew Lock rallied with two passing touchdowns in the third quarter to take the lead, improving to 3-0 as a starter for Seattle this season. Raiders star tight end Brock Bowers exited the loss with an ankle injury.

Follow along with Yahoo Sports for the latest NFL news, injury updates and more coming out of Week 10.

NFL Network's Ian Rapoport gave an update on some injuries to watch on Tuesday. It is still early in the practice week, but Rapoport mainly spoke about Kenneth Walker III and Baker Mayfield.

Walker missed last week's game due to a groin injury, but rookie Emmett Johnson balled out, so the Chiefs may not be rushing Walker back to the field.

Mayfield is coming off a bye, but was spotted in a walking boot last week at the facility. Rapoport said that he thinks Mayfield could miss this week's game, in which undrafted rookie QB Jalon Daniels would be back under center for Tampa Bay.

The Tennessee Titans are adding wide receiver Wan'Dale Robinson to injured reserve due to an ankle injury, per team reporter Jim Wyatt.

In a corresponding move, the team is signing wide receiver Xavier Restrepo to the active roster.

Robinson suffered the ankle injury in the team's Week 10 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars and could not return to the game. Restrepo was activated from the practice squad on game day and finished with 31 yards on three receptions.

Robinson has played in all nine games for Tennessee this season. He has brought in 38 receptions for 272 yards and a team-high three receiving touchdowns.

Head coach Robert Saleh has not revealed the extent of Robinson's ankle injury. If the wideout returns this season, he would first be eligible to be activated off IR in Week 15, ahead of the team's game against the Indianapolis Colts.

Tennessee will be without Robinson for at least the games against the Dallas Cowboys, Jacksonville Jaguars, Washington Commanders, and Detroit Lions.

Miami Dolphins defensive tackle Jordan Phillips suffered a torn biceps in last week's loss to the Indianapolis Colts that will sideline the 2025 fifth-round pick for the remainder of the season, according to ESPN's Marcel Louis-Jacques.

Phillips is the third Miami DT to sustain a season-ending injury in the past two weeks, per Louis-Jacques.

The Dolphins are 1-8 under first-year head coach Jeff Hafley. That said, their young core has flashed promise, especially on the defensive side of the ball.

The Commanders announced Tuesday that they are opening the 21-day practice window for running back Jacory Croskey-Merritt.

He has been sidelined due to a groin injury since Week 5. The running back remains on IR and must be activated before he can play in a game for Washington.

The Commanders take on the Cincinnati Bengals this week for "Monday Night Football," giving JCM an extra day of rest to get up to speed.

Croskey-Merritt has had a rather unproductive season so far, but at times has shown how effective he can be. Through five games, he has 239 yards and two touchdowns on 67 carries.

The NFL has utilized another flex to switch around the Week 12 schedule, per ESPN's Adam Schefter.

The New England Patriots and the Los Angeles Chargers were previously scheduled for that week's "Sunday Night Football" matchup.

With the injury to Patriots QB Drake Maye, and the Chargers' 1-8 start, the NFL has moved the game out of primetime.

New England-Los Angeles will now kick at 4:05 p.m. ET. Moving the Titans and Jaguars game into a 1 p.m. ET kick.

The new SNF kick will feature the Las Vegas Raiders taking on the Cleveland Browns.

The bye week came at a good time for Chicago. Wide receiver Luther Burden III was placed in the league's concussion protocol following the team's last game against the Buccaneers.

Coming out of the bye week, though, ESPN's Courtney Cronin reports that Burden has cleared concussion protocol.

Cronin also added that Kyler Gordon is considered "day-to-day" by head coach Ben Johnson due to a shoulder injury also suffered against the Buccaneers.

The Texans are on a short week this week, taking on the Colts on Thursday night in an AFC South divisional matchup.

It's a tough time for Houston to not have many days to get some much-needed rest, as the Texans are looking like they could be down some impactful players.

KPRC2 Houston's Aaron Wilson reported on Tuesday that defensive end Danielle Hunter, RB Woody Marks and WR Marvin Harrison Jr. are currently expected to miss Thursday night's game.

The good news for Texans fans is that running back David Montgomery was practicing, and it looks like he is in a good spot to start Thursday night for the first time since injuring his groin in Week 5.

The Cleveland Browns have been through this type of season before. It has just been a long time.

In 1979, the Browns had seven fourth-quarter drives to win games. In the 1980 season they were 11-5 and nine of the wins came by one score. That group got the nickname of the Kardiac Kids. Brian Sipe became a Cleveland legend, and won the 1980 NFL MVP award.

The 2026 Browns aren't at that level yet, but they're getting close. After rallying to beat the Houston Texans on a touchdown with 53 seconds left, the Browns are the first team in NFL history to win each of its first six games by four or fewer points, according to ESPN Insights. Every one of those wins has included a game-winning drive in the fourth quarter. It has been a magical, improbable run.

Al-Shaair suffered a groin injury in Week 3 that has kept him out of Week 4 and Week 10. He will reportedly require surgery, but he has not been ruled out for the season as of now.

The Texans have been hit with injuries at various points this season. Marvin Harrison Jr. (hamstring), Danielle Hunter (hamstring) and David Montgomery (groin) were among those who also missed Week 10. Montgomery has not played since Week 5.

Through seven games, the 29-year-old Al-Shaair has 26 solo tackles and 58 total tackles, plus three pass deflections.

Detroit Lions head coach Dan Campbell won't let one freak injury change how he approaches the game. Following star pass rusher Aidan Hutchinson tearing his ACL during a celebration, Campbell said he will not discourage other Lions players from celebrating big plays moving forward.

Campbell, who made those comments during an appearance on Detroit's 97.1 The Ticket, explained that Hutchinson's injury was "just one of those things," and that's not enough for Campbell to establish a "nobody celebrates anymore" rule.

"I hate it, I know he hates it. But I mean, the number of moves that I've seen Hutch make and the number of plyometrics, explosive movements, the spins, the one-leg lateral movements, lateral balances, I'm just like, it was one of those things, man," Campbell said. "I hate it. I think we all understand what it is, and let's be smart, but no, I'm not gonna say, 'Nobody celebrates anymore.'"

When asked whether he felt he would need to address the issue with the team, Campbell shot down that idea. He then revealed that he once sustained an injury while celebrating a big play.

The Vikings and Raiders' playoff hopes are trending in different directions.

Minnesota's chances of advancing to the postseason improved to 90% with its Sunday win, per Next Gen Stats, even as it sits in second place in a crowded NFC North. The Raiders' chances fell to 10% after their loss, their 4-6 record paired with their remaining schedule projecting worse chances than also-currently-out-of-it AFC contenders in the New England Patriots, Baltimore Ravens and Houston Texans.

A similarity between the two teams whose fates will be tied this season by their shared Cousins custody: the expectation of evolution as the offensive cast settles into its roles.

There are quarterbacks like Josh Allen and Patrick Mahomes, who achieve stardom and become synonymous with one team. There are quarterbacks like … well, we don't need to name them, but quarterbacks who never capitalize on their draft-day promise and fade into the ether. And then there's Kirk Cousins, whose career has swooped and swerved in a way he never can on the field.

From spare-parts draft pick to decade-long starter, from chain-wearing goof to one of the highest-paid players in the history of the sport, Cousins' career is a study in improbability, and naturally, he's just landed in the unlikeliest position of all — on track for true postseason success. You like that?

Jones would not elaborate with the hosts about the discussions regarding the Cowboys' defense and Parker's standing within the organization.

Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheim didn't directly support Parker on Monday, one day after a brutal showing from the Dallas defense in its 46-40 loss to the San Francisco 49ers.

Instead, he said everything is still under review.

"We're still working through the process, talking to the guys is the first step," Schottenheimer said, via The Dallas Morning News. "At the end of the day, there's a lot of things that we need to clean up as a football team. That starts with me."

The 26-year-old Joseph has not played this season due to a knee injury that limited him to only six games last season.

Barring a setback, Joseph, a 2024 First-team All-Pro, will be on the field when the Lions take on the Buccaneers in Week 11.

Dallas Cowboys right guard Tyler Booker sustained a high ankle sprain during the second quarter of Sunday's 46-40 loss to the San Francisco 49ers and is expected to miss at least four weeks, according to several reports.

Such an injury usually requires a recovery timeline of four to six weeks, but the Cowboys are hopeful that Booker can return in three to four weeks.

Starting cornerback DaRon Bland also suffered a right high ankle sprain during the Cowboys' first defensive series while trying to tackle 49ers receiver Deebo Samuel Sr. He had dealt with an injury to his left ankle during the previous week of practice.

The team is also considering whether or not to put both plalyers on injured reserve with a possible four-week absence. However, Dallas has a bye for Week 14, which could allow them to stay on the active roster.

The Chicago Bears should have running back Kyle Monangai available for Sunday's game against the New Orleans Saints.

Monangai has been out for more than a month with both a thumb injury and turf toe.

"It's something I can manage now," he said, via ESPN's Courtney Cronin. "The time off was needed though for sure. I feel in a much better spot than I was a month ago."

The two big Super Bowl odds movers this week resulted from one play on Sunday, when Aidan Hutchinson sacked Drake Maye and then Hutchinson proceeded to injure himself on the celebration.

Unfortunately, for the Lions, it's reportedly a torn ACL for Hutchinson, which would sideline him for the rest of the season. Detroit, despite a 7-2 record, moved from 18-1 to 20-1 odds to win the Super Bowl (11th-best odds). It's also reportedly a "significant lower-leg injury" for Maye, and with a 5-5 record already in a crowded AFC field, New England's Super Bowl odds tumbled from 28-1 entering the week to 66-1.

Chicago Bears, Jacksonville Jaguars: +750

Cincinnati Bengals, Kansas City Chiefs: 10-1

Denver Broncos, Minnesota Vikings, Seattle Seahawks: 16-1

New England Patriots, Pittsburgh Steelers: 66-1

Dallas Cowboys, Houston Texans, New York Giants, Tampa Bay Buccaneers: 80-1

The Chargers are bringing in some reinforcements ahead of a Monday night clash against the Ravens. The team announced Monday that they have activated tight end David Njoku and linebacker Denzel Perryman from injured reserve.

Njoku has been marked out with a fibula injury, while Perryman has been out with a pectoral injury. Both players were listed as "questionable" heading into this weekend, but were full participants in practice on Saturday.

In related moves, Los Angeles placed guard/tackle Branson Taylor on IR and elevated defensive lineman Myles Adams from the practice squad.

The 0-8 Chargers are trying to pick up their first win of the year against Baltimore.

The Raiders have some good news on star tight end Brock Bowers, who exited Sunday's loss to the Seahawks with an ankle injury. Though the injury, which occurred during the first quarter, initially appeared concerning, Las Vegas head coach Klint Kubiak said Monday that things were better than originally feared.

In a press conference, Kubiak said that the team was "still evaluating" Bowers, but that the tight end will be day-to-day with the injury.

"It's not as bad as we thought, but still is a significant injury, so we'll keep monitoring him," Kubiak said.

Bowers, who missed the first two games of the season after undergoing minor knee surgery, leads Las Vegas in receiving with 676 yards and six touchdowns in eight games.

New York Jets head coach Aaron Glenn was hired by the team thanks to his excellence as a defensive coordinator. But after the team struggled on defense during Glenn's first year as head coach, he decided to take over defensive play-calling duties in 2026.

That change lasted just nine games. Glenn told reporters Monday he gave up defensive play-calling ahead of the team's 31-12 loss to the Buffalo Bills in Week 10, per ESPN.

Glenn said the move was made to help the team win games. He added that while Jets defensive coordinator Brian Duker called plays Sunday, Glenn was "very involved" in the team's scheme.

"I've said this and I will continue to do this: Anything I can do as a head coach to help us win games, I'm willing to do it," Glenn said. "I'm not afraid to do that. So I gave him the lead, but I was very involved in what we ran."

The change appeared positive initially, as the Jets (2-8) gave up just 10 points in the first half Sunday. But Buffalo's offense got rolling in the second half, allowing the team to pull away.

The Jets ultimately gave up 31 points in a loss to the Bills. Though, in Duker's defense, facing Josh Allen in your first game as a defensive play-caller is among the toughest asks in the NFL. The Bills rank first in the NFL with 31.9 points scored per game. In that sense, Duker's defense actually held the team under its season-long average … barely. The Jets still allowed 31 points, so the team shouldn't start popping the champagne just yet.

#2605. Chiefs worked out K Matt Prater on Tuesday

The Chiefs worked out free agent kicker Matt Prater on Tuesday, according to the NFL’s personnel notice.

The team already has two veteran kickers, with Harrison Butker on the active roster and Justin Tucker on the practice squad. Butker is only 7-of-19 on field goal attempts this season.

His struggles prompted the Chiefs to sign Tucker on Oct. 28.

Butker had no field goal attempts in Sunday’s 35-12 win over the Falcons, but he did make all five extra points.

Prater, 42, has kicked for the Falcons (2007), Broncos (2007-13), Lions (2014-20), Cardinals (2021-24) and Bills (2025) in his 19-year career.

Last season for the Bills, Prater made 23-of-25 field goals and 46-of-49 extra points, including the postseason.

The Chiefs also worked out tight end John FitzPatrick, defensive tackle Aaron Graves, defensive tackle Eric Johnson and defensive tackle J.R. Singleton. FitzPatrick signed to the practice squad.

#2604. Rough Hawks injury news: CJ McCollum out 4 weeks (calf strain), Asa Newell likely out for season (toe)

This is rough injury news for Atlanta, which at 8-6 sits tied for the 4/5 seeds in the East:

• Guard CJ McCollum suffered a strained left calf and will be reevaluated in four weeks, the team announced.

• Big man Asa Newell has surgery to repair a left great toe hyperextension, and while the Hawks' announcement says he will be re-evaluated in four months, that will be mid-March, weeks away from the end of the regular season (April 11). It's unlikely we see Newell again this season.

After eight games as a starter to open the season, McCollum was moved to a bench role in favor of rookie Kingston Flemmings (who has made the most of that opportunity). McCollum has accepted and thrived in his bench role, averaging 14.9 points per game (scoring 20+ in each of his last three appearances), and shooting 37% from 3. Atlanta is going to miss his scoring punch off the bench.

Expect Corey Kispert to get extra run and touches with McCollum out.

Newell was poised for a bigger role this season after bouncing between the Hawks and their G League affiliate last season. However, he played in just five games this season before the toe injury and never really got the chance to show how much his game had grown. That said, the Hawks had already picked up his option for next season, so he isn't going anywhere.

Newell joins a few injured frontcourt Hawks players: Rookie center Henri Veesaar is out for the season with a torn ACL, while Mouhamed Gueye is out at least another month following foot surgery.

#2603. Rams Playoff Hopes Hyped by Super Bowl-Winning QB

Support Local Media - Click to Add LA Sports Report as a Preferred Source on Google

The Los Angeles Rams may have seen their superteam aspirations derailed by multiple injuries to key players, but their ultimate goal of a Super Bowl is still within reach.

A Super Bowl-winning quarterback recently revealed how he sees it happening.

Appearing on his "Set Hut!" podcast with Kyle Long, quarterback Russell Wilson made the case that a tough regular season can be salvaged by a deep playoff run.

Wilson explained that even with the Rams' 6-4 record putting them firmly on the bubble in terms of locking up a playoff spot, they're likely a team no opponent would want to play against in the postseason.

Largely, Wilson detailed, that's because of their superstars and the talent those players have to change the course of a game.

"Nobody in the National Football League wants to see the Rams sneak in," he said. "If your team, across the NFC or the AFC, you don't want to see the Rams sneak into the playoffs. Guess who they have? Myles Garrett, defensive player of the year. They also have Aaron Donald, defensive player of the year. They also have the MVP Matthew Stafford. They have player of the year-type candidates in Davante Adams and Puka Nacua."

The Rams' schedule, while daunting, also may allow them to right one of their biggest problems of the season during their upcoming bye this weekend.

The Rams face the Green Bay Packers on Thanksgiving Eve this season, but before that, they're off this Sunday.

Given the injuries to superstar receivers Adams and Nacua, that extra time off could be hugely beneficial, even if it only helps Nacua get "a little bit of extra treatment" and Adams "a little bit healthier."

"If I'm Puka Nacua, if I'm Davante Adams, I'm doing whatever it takes," Wilson said. "I'm flying all the treatment in, I'm having all the best people, whatever it is, I'm making sure I'm getting the best of the best treatment. I'm using the Rams training staff to help me out too. I'm spending all my time there."

In Wilson's view, working through a few days off now could make all the difference in the playoffs, and there will be plenty of time to rest once the season is done.

"You know what's better than a bye week? Winning a Super Bowl. Getting back in the playoffs and winning a Super Bowl and having the time to do whatever you want afterwards," Wilson said. "That's what I'm doing over the next couple of weeks."

Do you think the Rams stars would be smart to use the off week to get healthier ahead of the playoffs?
