#2602. NFL Power Rankings entering Week 11: Can the Browns keep winning in dramatic fashion?

NFC East: Cowboys | Giants | Eagles | Commanders NFC North: Bears | Lions | Packers | Vikings NFC South: Falcons | Panthers | Saints | Buccaneers NFC West: Cardinals | Rams | 49ers | Seahawks

AFC East: Bills | Dolphins | Patriots | Jets AFC North: Ravens | Bengals | Browns | Steelers AFC South: Texans | Colts | Jaguars | Titans AFC West: Broncos | Chiefs | Raiders | Chargers

The Cleveland Browns have been through this type of season before. It has just been a long time.

In 1979, the Browns had seven fourth-quarter drives to win games. In the 1980 season they were 11-5 and nine of the wins came by one score. That group got the nickname of the Kardiac Kids. Brian Sipe became a Cleveland legend, and won the 1980 NFL MVP award.

The 2026 Browns aren't at that level yet, but they're getting close. After rallying to beat the Houston Texans on a touchdown with 53 seconds left, the Browns are the first team in NFL history to win each of its first six games by four or fewer points, according to ESPN Insights. Every one of those wins has included a game-winning drive in the fourth quarter. It has been a magical, improbable run.

"We're going to figure something out about starting a hell of a lot faster," Browns head coach Todd Monken said, according to the team's transcripts. "But our guys continue to fight, and they battle, and they don't, they don't blink. Which is probably more important than starting fast, is when you have guys that continue to fight."

Whether it's sustainable might be irrelevant. Suddenly, the 6-4 Browns are in great shape to make the playoffs.

With the New England Patriots likely in for a big drop after Drake Maye's ankle injury and the Browns knocking the Texans back while also clinching the head-to-head tiebreaker, Cleveland's playoff hopes got a lot brighter Sunday. There was another assist on Monday night, when the previously winless Chargers beat the Ravens, knocking Baltimore back to 4-6. The Browns would be the seventh seed if the season ended today and they're a game up on any other team in the running. It's hard to find a team behind them — Patriots, Ravens, Raiders, Texans — that's going to make a big push. Three of those teams' quarterbacks are either injured or traded and 3-6 Houston is miles behind now because of the tiebreaker.

In Week 1, the Browns were blown out 34-10 by the Jaguars and there were plenty of jokes about how they were already tanking for a quarterback. Now Cleveland is 6-4 heading into a well deserved bye week.

"Isn't that cool? Isn't that awesome?" Monken said. "I mean, holy s***. There's no other way to put it, man."

There are still seven games to go and like Monken said, the Browns have to figure out how to play better in the first three quarters of games to win enough to get a playoff berth. But they have already stacked six wins and are in the clear lead for a wild-card spot. Cleveland fans couldn't have expected a playoff berth, but a fun start to the season has the Browns well within range.

Here are the NFL power rankings after Week 10:

One of the signs of a good team is the ability to blow out bad teams. The Jaguars' 40-23 win over the Titans was their fifth win this season by 17 or more points, and it came with Jacksonville gambling that it could give trade additions defensive tackle Jordan Davis and safety Jessie Bates III the week off. In more than half of Jacksonville's games, it has throttled its opponent. The Jags' point differential of +125 is 37 points better than the Bills, who are second.

The Jaguars haven't played a tough schedule, but it actually gets easier. Their remaining games against teams with a winning record come against the Giants, Bears and Steelers. The Jaguars are going to put up a very good record and are just hoping the other top teams in the AFC, most notably Buffalo, lose some.

The 49ers cooked the Cowboys' defense, putting up 46 points and 584 yards. Dallas' defense is dreadful but it's still hard to pile up close to 600 yards in any NFL game.

The way the 49ers have climbed to the top of the NFL in yards per game is worth studying. Brock Purdy was famously Mr. Irrelevant in the draft and now he's an MVP candidate. Christian McCaffrey was at a point in which age and touches should have started to chip away at his effectiveness, but he is tied for the NFL lead with 13 total touchdowns. Draft experts laughed at the Kaelon Black pick in the third round; he's one of the best backup running backs in the league. Deebo Samuel Sr.'s career looked like it might be over after last season, but he has five touchdowns in six games. The 49ers had to give up only a sixth-round draft pick for Keenan Allen in a trade and he had five catches for 61 yards on Sunday.

The conclusion: Kyle Shanahan is your NFL Coach of the Year.

Beating the Jets doesn't seem to be that impressive, but it was to Bills head coach Joe Brady. His explanation made sense once he laid out that Buffalo had short rest before a road game after beating a great Vikings defense in Minneapolis last Monday night.

"This is the best win we've had this season," Brady said, via the team's site.

"We're getting back real early Tuesday morning [from Minnesota] to be able to reset and get their bodies ready to go to go back on the road."

It absolutely was impressive for the Bills to win 31-12 in a letdown spot, no matter the competition. The Bills host the Dolphins this weekend before a big showdown against the Chiefs on Thanksgiving.

The Bengals' performance Sunday night might have been the most impressive of the NFL season. Critics doubted the Steelers' 6-2 start, but they ranked sixth in DVOA coming into Sunday night's game. And the Bengals made them look like a bottom-feeding Conference USA opponent in town for homecoming. The Bengals outgained the Steelers 337-40 in the first half, which shouldn't happen against any competent NFL team. Cincinnati looked like a legitimate Super Bowl contender. It now ranks No. 1 in DVOA this season.

Joe Burrow had 302 passing yards and three touchdowns by halftime. If the Steelers had kept it competitive, Burrow might have challenged Norm Van Brocklin's longstanding NFL record of 554 passing yards in a game. Burrow finished with 409 passing yards. When asked what kind of quarterback he was on Sunday night, Burrow said, "A great one." The Bengals are feeling good, and rightfully so. The biggest key might be the offensive line, which allowed one sack on 46 dropbacks from Burrow.

"They've been unbelievable," Burrow said, via the team's transcripts.

The Bears didn't do anything wrong on their bye week. They didn't "move down." The Bengals just moved up after one of the most impressive games of the season.

Lingering for the Bears is their home defeat to the Vikings in Week 2. They lost 9-3, and based on how the Vikings looked with Kirk Cousins in Week 10, that could be a problem. The Bears play at Minnesota in Week 18 and that's looking like an early candidate to be flexed to the final Sunday night slot.

Chicago is 0-2 in the division (Minnesota is 3-1) and that could also be bad for tiebreakers. The Lions suffered a massive injury to Aidan Hutchinson on Sunday and the Packers lost ground with a bad loss, so the NFC North could evolve into a two-team race. And the Bears might need to win in Minneapolis in Week 18 to take the division.

The Vikings blew out the Packers without three key players: linebacker Blake Cashman, receiver Jordan Addison and tight end T.J. Hockenson. Kirk Cousins is 38 and there should be skepticism whether he can turn the Vikings into a Super Bowl threat, but everything looked much better in Week 10. And receiver Justin Jefferson had a surprisingly self-aware comment on where the Vikings stand.

"All we as an offense have to do is be mediocre at this point," Jefferson said, via The Athletic. "The defense is creating so much pressure."

He's not wrong. The Vikings were fierce on Sunday, pressuring Jordan Love 22 times on 35 dropbacks, according to Pro Football Focus. Love was sacked eight times. The Vikings weren't tremendous on offense with 312 yards, but as Jefferson pointed out, that might be enough.

The Chiefs also didn't do anything to "move down" in a thorough 35-13 win over the Falcons. The Vikings needed to be adjusted after seeing them play well with Kirk Cousins. At this point it's fair to wonder if the Chiefs are being underrated, which is strange for a team that has been in the spotlight so much over the Patrick Mahomes era. There isn't much evidence to suggest they should be higher. They're eighth in DVOA. They're sixth in Super Bowl odds. They're sixth in offensive and defensive EPA. They're clearly good, but are they Super Bowl contender good?

A big piece of that answer could be Josh Downs. He had four catches for 53 yards and a touchdown just five days after he was traded to the Chiefs. Xavier Worthy was shut out, and we can finally close the book on him making any meaningful impact. It's just not going to happen. The Chiefs need something extra in the offense, and perhaps it's Downs, who always seemed to have more potential and the Colts couldn't unlock it. Mahomes had 348 passing yards and five touchdowns on Sunday and perhaps that's a sign of a hot streak coming.

It's hard to find an advanced metric that indicates the Broncos should be higher than this. They're 14th in point differential, ninth in DVOA, 15th in net EPA as of last week and also a stunning 30th in yards per game on offense and 27th in yards allowed per game on defense. Their Super Bowl odds are tied for ninth best, for what that's worth. But here's why that doesn't matter: Denver is 7-2 after stacking (close) wins and has the easiest remaining schedule in the NFL, via DVOA, after playing the hardest schedule to this point in the season.

Here's what Denver has coming up: vs. Raiders, at Steelers, vs. Dolphins, at Jets, at Raiders, vs. Bills, at Patriots, vs. Chargers. That's two playoff contenders (assuming Drake Maye's injury sinks the Patriots) of eight remaining games. Like last season, the Broncos could end up with 13 or 14 wins and an army of naysayers wondering how good they really are.

The Sam Darnold/Drew Lock debate is flawed. Lock's three starts came twice against the Cardinals and vs. the Raiders. Arizona and Las Vegas have two of the worst defenses in the NFL. Still, Lock has played well and Darnold has been prone to turnovers. Lock hasn't thrown an interception and Darnold has nine despite missing three games and almost all of a fourth. But there isn't any indication from Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald that he's considering a change.

"Drew's been fantastic," Macdonald said Monday on Seattle Sports 710, via the Seattle Times. "Drew's been phenomenal. But Sam's our quarterback."

That's the correct answer. Lock has played well and if Darnold continues to struggle, the Seahawks can turn to him later in the season. It would be premature to make a switch based on three games against bad opponents.

The Rams have won four in a row. They're still more likely than not to miss the playoffs — 44.2% chance to make it, via DVOA — because they have by far the NFL's toughest remaining schedule. But the Rams played well, albeit against a bad Cardinals team using rookie quarterback Carson Beck in his first career start. The Rams won 34-6 by running it 46 times for 202 yards. Konata Mumpfield provided some hope at receiver with Puka Nacua and Davante Adams out, with three catches for 81 yards. L.A.'s defense limited Arizona to six first downs.

It's still a hard path to the playoffs because of the schedule and injuries, but the Rams are hanging around.

"I think it's really tested our team," head coach Sean McVay said of having to find injury replacements. "But it's also shown there's a lot of guys that are capable of, hey let's instill belief and then let's go have that confidence earned through evidence."

The Lions' season changed with the reported ACL injury to defensive end Aidan Hutchinson. They were already without linebacker Jack Campbell, arguably the second-best player on the defense, and Detroit lost its unquestioned star because of a sack celebration. That's brutal. Derrick Moore and DJ Wonnum are capable vets and will fill in, but they're nowhere near Hutchinson's level.

"Any time you lose a player of his caliber, the type of teammate he is — he's a captain of ours — that doesn't make things easy," Lions head coach Dan Campbell said, according to NFL.com.

The Lions won on Sunday without Hutchinson for most of the game to improve to 7-2, and perhaps they have enough wins banked to make the playoffs in what will be a difficult wild-card race. But their hopes of being a Super Bowl contender are likely dashed without their two best defensive players.

The Packers' bye comes at a good time. They were playing very well before Sunday, when they were crushed at home by the Vikings. The break gives the Packers a chance to regroup, and also perhaps get Micah Parsons back for a game against the Rams the day before Thanksgiving. The Packers should rightly believe that Parsons will transform their team upon his return.

But there are concerns after Sunday. The offensive line was in shambles against the Vikings after showing improvement over a few weeks. The Vikings are a tough matchup, but Jordan Love can't get hit 12 times. The running game also disappeared without Josh Jacobs as Green Bay had just 56 yards on 17 carries. There are some things to clean up before a massive game in the wild-card race against the Rams.

Was Sunday's outing just a bad night against a hot Bengals team or a bad sign for the Steelers going forward? It's OK to excuse it as a one-off. Before the 38-18 blowout loss, the Steelers were 6-2 and showing improvement. It's also OK to worry that Pittsburgh was exposed, though Aaron Rodgers didn't think so when asked if the loss changes the season's trajectory.

"That's very dramatic," Rodgers said, via the team's site. "I've been a part of this league for a long time. There's big wins, there's tough losses, so we'll deal with this properly."

One thing that is an issue for the Steelers is their receiver room. DK Metcalf continued to have minimal impact, as he was held without a catch before garbage time in the fourth quarter. Germie Bernard was blanked and has just 57 yards in Pittsburgh's last three games. No other healthy receiver on the roster has more than 39 yards this season. Roman Wilson and Michael Pittman Jr. could both return in the next couple weeks, and that is badly needed.

One developing story is what to do with Deshaun Watson. Those who log quarterback wins will say he is 6-3 this season. That's misguided, but many people follow that logic. Watson is 20th in adjusted EPA per play and he has a middling 89.1 passer rating. That's 20th among quarterbacks with at least 100 attempts. The Browns have had some fun comeback wins and it will be interesting to see if Cleveland overreacts to that and extends Watson, whose contract has been one of the worst in the NFL.

Certainly, the Browns would rather not have to come back and win every game, as they've been doing.

"I wish collectively him and I together would play better early and coach better early and we didn't have to get to this," Browns head coach Todd Monken said, via the team's transcripts. "And it's not just been them. It's been our team, last week the same way."

The Buccaneers looked to have a tough four-game stretch after the bye when the schedule came out. It has gotten much easier. Their next four opponents are the Lions (lost Aidan Hutchinson and Jack Campbell to injuries between Weeks 8 and 10), Panthers (lost three in a row before a win Sunday), Chargers (a stunningly bad start to the season) and Ravens (lost quarterbacks Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley to injuries). That's why forecasting schedule strength can be difficult.

Now the Buccaneers have to take advantage of their good fortune. They're up to a 60.9% chance to win the division, via DVOA, in part because their defense ranks first in the NFL in that metric and they have the third-easiest remaining schedule.

The Giants are still in fine shape to win the NFC East because the Cowboys seem incapable of getting a stop on defense and the Commanders are flawed too. But blowing Thursday night's game against Washington keeps the pressure on them. The Giants had two chances to put the game away with the lead but went three-and-out each time. Then J.J. McCarthy threw an interception to end the game.

Otherwise, McCarthy played pretty well. He was 23-of-36 passing for 293 yards. Since Week 6, which was his first significant playing time with the Giants, he's 10th in adjusted EPA per play among quarterbacks with at least 100 plays. He hasn't been perfect but he's still young, and joining a team in-season and becoming a starter is a tough assignment.

"I thought he played very well," Giants head coach John Harbaugh said after the loss to the Commanders, according to the team's transcripts. "I mean, there were some plays made, he made some throws, scrambled. I thought J.J. played very well."

The Panthers paid edge rusher Jaelan Phillips $120 million over four years, and at that price point Phillips should be one of the biggest impact players in the NFL. On Sunday, he finally was. Phillips had three tackles for loss, including a sack, and the Panthers tied their season best by allowing 222 yards in a win over the Saints.

The Panthers' defense, along with a huge game from running back Chuba Hubbard, was the difference in a major victory in the NFC South race. It was Phillips' first game back after missing three due to a hamstring injury.

"Obviously there's been a lot of adversity, a lot of change, things happening, and we deserve some good things happening to us, so it was really good to get out there and play well." Phillips said, via the team's site.

Sunday was the fifth time this season that the Texans have given up a drive in the final minutes of regulation or overtime to lose a game. Houston was supposed to be one of the best defenses in the NFL. The Texans were second in EPA per play allowed last season. This season they're 20th, despite having mostly the same personnel and coaches.

While defensive success can fluctuate from season to season more than offensive success, the Texans' decline is perplexing. If Houston finished just two of those five games, it would be above .500.

"We have to play better — run defense, have to tackle better," head coach DeMeco Ryans said, via Texans Wire.

Fernando Mendoza made plenty of mistakes in his first NFL start, but he faced a Seattle defense that is among the top three in the NFL. Mendoza was 17-of-29 passing for 143 yards, and the biggest issue was that he took six sacks.

Mendoza will get better, though his next two matchups are also tough at Denver and at Cleveland. The schedule will get easier, but one of the concerns of the Kirk Cousins trade was shoving Mendoza into the lineup during a very difficult stretch. That was evident during a tough matchup against Seattle.

"It's good to get punched in the face, because now it's a great opportunity to grow and learn and to really unveil all the deficiencies that I have in my game, as a future hopeful leader of this offense," Mendoza said, via the Raiders' site.

Linebacker Sonny Styles is going to make a case for Defensive Rookie of the Year. Against the Giants, the seventh overall pick of the draft had 13 tackles. His biggest tackle came on a third-and-3 right after the two-minute warning when he shot through for a tackle for loss on a J.J. McCarthy designed quarterback run. Styles read that play because the Giants had run it in Week 5, which is high-level awareness from a rookie.

That tackle allowed Washington to get the ball back, and Jayden Daniels led a game-winning drive that kept the Commanders' season alive. Styles is up to 80 tackles on the season and he is used often as a blitzer. He has one interception and one sack. He is looking like a great first-round pick.

The Patriots took a big drop in the rankings and it might not be far enough. Drake Maye suffered what the Patriots fear is a fractured ankle, per ESPN. At the very least he'll be out a while and the most likely outcome seems to be that his season is over.

That turns the offense over to Tommy DeVito. It has been a long time since he had a few decent games as a rookie for the Giants in 2023 and became a fleeting cult figure. He looked entirely overmatched Sunday after Maye left the game. He had 81 yards on 24 attempts against a bad Lions defense. It's hard to see how the Patriots keep their season afloat without Maye, unless DeVito somehow plays way better than he did Sunday or the Patriots find some very unexpected help off the street.

There's not much more that can be said about the Cowboys' defense. Even noted Cowboys fan Post Malone was absolutely fed up. After allowing 584 yards in a 46-40 loss to the 49ers, Brian Schottenheimer made perhaps his harshest comments on the team since becoming head coach.

"I thought the second half was unacceptable," Schottenheimer said, according to the team's site. "Tackling was atrocious. We're going to do a deep dive and see why."

It's not like the Cowboys' offense has been the 1999 Rams or anything: fifth in points scored, eighth in yards gained, fifth in EPA per play and sixth in DVOA. That still should be enough to win a poor division. The defense is ruining the Cowboys' season, though DVOA still gives Dallas a 32.4% chance to win the NFC East.

The Ravens lost but can't put all the blame on quarterback injuries. Jacoby Brissett had 340 yards and mostly played well. But the running game was invisible on Monday night against the Chargers. Derrick Henry had just 10 yards on 10 carries. Baltimore's defense wasn't good enough, allowing Los Angeles to rush for a season-best 160 yards. The Ravens have lost five in a row and are in a bad place the rest of the season.

The AFC wild-card race is soft, but it's not like the Ravens are looking like much of a threat. They just lost a home game to a Chargers team that was 0-8 coming in. Even if Lamar Jackson heals quickly, it seems like there won't be any reason for him to return late in the season.

The Saints' next three games are at Chicago, at Cincinnati and vs. Green Bay. This could get bad for New Orleans, which is showing that last season's strong second half was a fluke fueled by a weak schedule. The Panthers have allowed less than 300 yards this season four times: vs. the Cooper Rush-led Falcons, vs. the Browns, vs. the Tanner McKee-led Eagles and on Sunday against the Saints. New Orleans had just 222 yards of offense. There were offensive line injuries but it was still a poor performance and a bad home loss.

"Yeah, [coach Kellen Moore] was upset, and rightfully so," Saints quarterback Tyler Shough said via the team's transcripts. "As players, I think we failed him. As coach, I think we had those moments where we had a couple third downs, and I could have found Chris [Olave] or made a play there. We had those opportunities, and he's obviously frustrated. We have to find a way to win that game."

If there was a positive it was seeing a healthy Jordyn Tyson, the Saints' first-round draft pick, grab 11 passes for 80 yards as Carolina focused its coverage on Olave.

In Weeks 3 and 4, with Michael Penix Jr. back in the lineup, the Falcons blew out the Packers and Saints and looked like a potential division winner. Other than those two games, the Falcons are 1-7. Whatever happened in those games was a complete outlier. Atlanta averaged 459 yards in those two games and hasn't been above 370 yards in any other game this season. Bijan Robinson hasn't rushed for more than 100 yards in a game since that Week 4 win at New Orleans.

On Sunday the defense completely let down, days after the team traded safety Jessie Bates III to the Jaguars. Patrick Mahomes had 348 yards and five touchdowns and Kansas City scored 35 points without running back Kenneth Walker III.

"All of this falls on me," Falcons head coach Kevin Stefanski said, via the team's site. "So, I'll take responsibility for everything that goes on in this football team. We all have to be better; that's the truth."

Everyone got way too excited for rookie quarterback Carson Beck because of one solid performance in the Hall of Fame Game. The overreaction to that was fierce. Beck, in his first game since then (he missed the rest of the preseason with a rib injury), had 108 yards and a 38.4 passer rating. Arizona had just six first downs and didn't score a touchdown. Beck had a tough matchup against the Rams and the Cardinals had many injuries on offense. Sunday was still a reality check. Beck could be a good player, but it's going to take time.

"It was a rough day, and that's probably a nice way of saying it, for the offense," Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur said, via the team's site, though he also said he "was impressed" with Beck.

The good news for Beck is the Cardinals aren't going anywhere and have no other option at quarterback the rest of the way. They'll get seven more games to evaluate Beck and he'll have some easier matchups. Arizona will know whether it has its quarterback for 2027 or needs to draft another one.

The Colts can win without their fans being conflicted because the team doesn't have its own 2027 first-round pick. Something that made no sense at the trade deadline and made less sense Sunday is why Indianapolis didn't deal away running back Jonathan Taylor. The Colts had reported offers of a second- and fifth-round pick for Taylor and they passed. Yet, the Colts split the backfield between Taylor and Seth McGowan again Sunday, with Taylor getting 16 carries and McGowan 12. The Colts could get a committee back for much cheaper than a second-round pick. As for the idea of not wearing out Taylor in a lost season, do they think they'll be a playoff contender next season? Seems unlikely.

The other part of the Colts' season that is hard to believe is how bad Daniel Jones has been. Jones had 108 yards and a 41.5 passer rating against a bad Dolphins defense. Jones has the lowest passer rating of any regular starting quarterback in the NFL this season, at 67. That's a 33-point drop from last season, which is stunning even accounting for injuries and trades.

Kyle McCord wasn't all that bad against the Colts in his first NFL start. He easily outplayed his counterpart, Daniel Jones. He was 17-of-32 passing for 209 yards and he ran for a touchdown. McCord also lost a fumble that was recovered in the end zone for a touchdown. Dolphins head coach Jeff Hafley said he was impressed with how McCord bounced back afterward.

"He didn't blink. He just stayed composed," Hafley said, according to the team's transcripts. "Coming out of the half, I mean, that thing could have gotten ugly and the game could have gotten away from us when he fumbled the ball and they scored, and he just kept responding the whole entire time."

McCord has at least a few more weeks to show what he can do in the NFL as Malik Willis is on injured reserve. With a little more improvement he can perhaps carve out a role as a reliable backup.

Cam Ward has improved, and Titans head coach Robert Saleh revealed Monday that the team gave Ward more responsibility at the line of scrimmage before Week 7. In the three games since, the Titans' scoring average has spiked from 14 points per game to 27.7, and that came against three good defenses (Browns, Bengals, Jaguars). Ward has three games this season with a passer rating above 83 and two of them came since the philosophical change.

The Titans are in the middle of a lost season, but a strong second half from Ward can offer renewed hope for the future.

"To be fair to Cam, we've said from the beginning we were going to give him every opportunity to prove that he is a franchise quarterback of the Tennessee Titans," Saleh said, via the team's site. "So, philosophically, the change was: How are we going to evaluate whether or not he is capable of being our franchise quarterback if we don't give him the opportunity to prove it? And I think over the last three weeks he has done that. Or, at least is doing it."

Not much has gone right for the Eagles this season, but the A.J. Brown trade looks to be a win for them. Brown has been stunningly bad for the Patriots. A high ankle sprain suffered in Week 1 has contributed to his quiet season. Overall, New England can't be happy to have just 11 catches and 128 yards from a receiver who will be 30 years old next season and cost the Patriots a 2028 first-round draft pick.

The Eagles are positioned well in the next two drafts, with extra first-round picks in 2027 and 2028 and extra second-round picks in 2028 and 2029, because of the trades of Jordan Davis, Cam Jurgens and Brown. That might not make the rest of this season any more palatable but Philadelphia should be able to reload quickly.

When Aaron Glenn said he was taking over defensive play-calling this season, he said calling plays was his "superpower." On Sunday, he gave up the "lead" play-calling duties to defensive coordinator Brian Duker, which practically means that Glenn is no longer the play-caller. Not that Jets fans needed another sign that Glenn won't be back in 2027 as New York's head coach, but that adds to the list.

The next big question will be when to flip the QB1 job to rookie Cade Klubnik from veteran Geno Smith. Klubnik got some playing time after Smith injured his ankle Sunday, and a 2-8 team should be thinking about getting a look at a rookie and benching a 36-year-old who will be a free agent after the season. Glenn said that's not a consideration yet.

"Geno's our starter," Glenn said Monday, via ESPN. "Come on now, let's not do that.

"I think Geno's had a really good year and it would be disrespectful to him to just [replace him]. I think we all understand that. I think we all know that he's our starter."

The Chargers got the win they needed to avoid a lot of annoying 0-17 questions. Let's not get too far ahead of ourselves; it was just one win, and on the whole, they've still been the NFL's worst team this season. But give the Chargers credit for a good effort. They figured out how to make the Ravens one-dimensional. Baltimore had 16 yards rushing on 15 carries. That forced Baltimore to lean too much on quarterback Jacoby Brissett, who was making his first Ravens start after being traded less than two weeks ago.

It was also encouraging to see Omarion Hampton emerge with a 105-yard rushing day. Justin Herbert completed only 12 passes but he didn't need to do much more because the running game was effective. Maybe the Chargers can build on their first win and have a respectable second half of the season.

#2601. Lakers’ trust in starter’s defensive gambles paying off

Matisse Thybulle's explanation for how he steals passes midair while opponents try to get the ball up the court is simple.

Even if the act of stealing the pass like a free safety intercepts a quarterback isn't.

Los Angeles Lakers guard Matisse Thybulle (4) steals the ball from the Sacramento Kings during an NBA game, Wednesday, Nov. 4, 2026, in Sacramento, Calif. AP Photo/Scott Marshall

"I just look at the person passing; I just make eye contact with them," Thybulle said after Tuesday's shootaround ahead of the Lakers' home game against the Hornets. "Because most guys aren't really throwing no-look passes. Like Luka [Dončić], [Nikola] Jokić, there's a couple guys in the league who really throw nowhere passes, especially in transition.

"So if you just look people in their eyes, they're going to look where they're throwing the ball. I can just get a sense from the eye contact."

Matisse Thybulle of the Los Angeles Lakers blocks a shot by Devin Booker of the Phoenix Suns on Sunday, Nov. 15, 2026, in Phoenix, Arizona. Getty Images

But if everyone was able to pick off passes like Thybulle, who's shown a knack for playing the passing lanes throughout his eight-year NBA career, then they would.

So what makes him more equipped at picking off passes in a way that looks easy?

"Just being willing to take the risk," he said. "I've missed a bunch of gambles as well as getting some. So just being willing to take the risk of assuming that where they're looking is in fact where the guy is trying to pass the ball to."

The Lakers have benefited from the defensive gambles the 6-foot-5 wing takes.

They entered Tuesday leading the league in defensive turnover percentage (18.7), according to Cleaning The Glass, and Thybulle is a significant reason.

He entered Tuesday ranked No. 2 in the league in total steals (31) and deflections (60).

Giannis Antetokounmpo shoots against Matisse Thybulle, left, and Austin Reaves during an NBA basketball game Monday, Nov. 2, 2026, in Los Angeles. AP Photo/Jayne Kamin-Oncea

"Me and [assistant] coach Greg [St. Jean] have talked a lot about that — just trying to find ways for me to be me within the foundation of our defense," Thybulle said. "And they like me gambling because it generates turnovers, whether I'm getting the steal. It's just a matter of doing it in ways where our defense can absorb the mistake, if you will. If I do it in ways where our defense is structured to be able to absorb it, then it's something that we can just use, and I try to use to give us an advantage."

The Lakers empowering Thybulle to take advantage of his defensive freedom, similar to how Dončić takes advantage of his offensive freedom, goes back to trust that was established during the preseason and training camp.

"It can be challenging at times to play with someone like me who's taking a lot of risks, gambling, getting out of position and sometimes throwing off the team defense," he said. "And it can be really easy for them to just be like, 'Well, Matisse keeps messing up our defense. Like, what the hell is he doing?' But they understand and they let me learn from my mistakes."

He continued: "I gamble and sometimes I don't get the pass, but sometimes I get a steal on the back end. There's just the rapport that's grown through that."

#2600. Clifton soccer legend leads N.J. program to shot at first state title

WALDWICK – Teddy Niziolek learned how to win big at Clifton.

Now he's built something of his own at Verona.

The Hillbillies moved one step closer to their first state title Wednesday, beating Waldwick, 1-0, on the road in the Group 1 girls soccer semifinals. Sophomore Ella Prieto scored late in the first half and Verona hung on for its fourth shutout in five games.

Verona (14-3-2) will face Haddon Township on Saturday, hoping to finish what it couldn't a year ago in its first appearance in the state final.

"One of our biggest goals was to make it back in the final," Niziolek said. "The girls have been working hard all season, every game. We play with high intensity, high energy. Today wasn't one of our best performances, but great teams know how to dig deep and find a way to win."

The trip back to Franklin High School continues a steady rise under Niziolek, a former Clifton standout who won three county championships playing for legendary coach Fernando Rossi. Named North Jersey's Boys Soccer Player of the Decade for the 2000s, he went on to play four seasons at Seton Hall before being drafted by the Columbus Crew.

In 2021, he inherited a program that managed only one winning season in the previous six years. Since then, the Hillbillies have averaged more than 12 victories per season and captured back-to-back sectional championships.

"The biggest thing is the culture," Niziolek said. "We're a culture that's built on family, being together, work ethic, being strong. My goal is to try to get the most out of these girls."

Verona has been nearly unstoppable in the state tournament, outscoring its five opponents 23-1. But on Wednesday, the Hillbillies leaned on their defense and an unlikely source to grind out a victory.

Verona broke through with a well-constructed sequence in the 32nd minute.

Natalia Ross found space in the attacking third and slipped a pass to Emma Smith, who spotted Prieto alone in front. The sophomore settled herself and drove a shot into the left side for a 1-0 lead.

It was Prieto's second goal in as many games after she entered the state tournament with just one goal on the season.

"It's definitely a little crazy. I'm really proud," Prieto said. "But our whole team has been working for this. It's not just one person."

The Hillbillies have made a habit of putting games away during their postseason run. Wednesday offered a reminder that their defense can be just as important as their attack.

Verona has surrendered only 13 goals in 19 games, with senior Morgan Rossi anchoring a back line with Marley McDevitt and Ally Romanyshyn.

"Our teammates are our family," said Rossi, one of only three senior starters. "We see each other every single day and we hang out off of the field. We hit the field, we all want it together."

Senior goalkeeper and Davidson commit Molly Daggs only needed to make one save to secure the shutout. For much of the afternoon, she was largely a spectator.

Verona lost to Shore Regional, 2-1, in last year's Group 1 championship game. That experience has remained a source of motivation for a young team that brought back nine starters.

Niziolek has emphasized staying even-keeled through the highs and lows of another successful season.

"We remember that feeling, and we just want to overcome that and hopefully bring it home," Prieto said.

This article originally appeared on NorthJersey.com: Clifton soccer legend leads N.J. program to shot at first state title

#2599. Week 11 Chicago Bears power rankings roundup

The Chicago Bears are back in action following the bye week. It was great for the Bears to pause and have a chance to get healthy, but now is where the stakes are really going to go up.

The schedule is full of playoff-hopeful teams, and that includes four more games against the NFC North gauntlet.

Much is being made of Chicago's Super Bowl chances after their 7-2 start. Now they actually have to go out and prove it.

Let's see where the Bears rank heading into their final eight games.

Second-Half Outlook: Survive a brutal schedule down the stretch and hope that Jeffery Simmons continues to be a difference-maker

Once dubbed a prime regression candidate heading into the regular season, the Bears have survived without Caleb Williams for three games and somehow continue to play much better defense than the numbers suggest. Williams' Year 3 jump has been notable, even with a four-interception game in Week 9. The talent on offense is evident, and their ceiling feels safe with Ben Johnson calling plays. How far they go this season will come down to the defense, especially the secondary. We'll see if not making another move at the deadline comes back to bite them.

The Athletic – Chad Graff and Josh Kendall

Ben Johnson was bullish about his second-year wide receiver in the preseason, and we're seeing why. Burden is 16th in the league with 644 receiving yards, and 385 of those came in his last four games. From weeks 6 through 9, he had more receiving yards than all but five players in the league, and he got 23.5 percent of the Bears' passing targets. That last number may go up as the season progresses.

Bears (No. 5; 7-2): They can't afford to overlook the Saints, four days before a showdown with the Lions.

The Bears didn't do anything wrong on their bye week. They didn't "move down." The Bengals just moved up after one of the most impressive games of the season.

Lingering for the Bears is their home defeat to the Vikings in Week 2. They lost 9-3, and based on how the Vikings looked with Kirk Cousins in Week 10, that could be a problem. The Bears play at Minnesota in Week 18 and that's looking like an early candidate to be flexed to the final Sunday night slot.

Chicago is 0-2 in the division (Minnesota is 3-1) and that could also be bad for tiebreakers. The Lions suffered a massive injury to Aidan Hutchinson on Sunday and the Packers lost ground with a bad loss, so the NFC North could evolve into a two-team race. And the Bears might need to win in Minneapolis in Week 18 to take the division.

6. Chicago Bears (4) Having spent last week on a bye, the Bears didn't do anything wrong — they just got caught up in a Power Rankings shakeup, with a couple of impressive teams leap-frogging them. Last time out, Chicago earned a narrow win over Tampa Bay that exposed some weaknesses but also felt like an anomaly in the larger picture. I still have plenty of confidence in this team, but it has to navigate the incredibly competitive NFC North to fulfill its potential. The Bears need to come out of the break on the right foot, facing a three-week stretch that includes dates with Detroit and Jacksonville.

3. Chicago Bears (3): An offense that runs the ball more than any other in the league is about to get RB Kyle Monangai back − which is akin to making a trade deadline acquisition for free.

Non-QB MVP at midseason: RB D'Andre Swift

The Bears have maintained a top-five rushing offense (142 yards per game) despite a constant wave of injuries in the backfield. A big reason for that is the load Swift has carried in Kyle Monangai's five-game absence (toe/thumb). Swift has logged the third-most offensive snaps of any Bears skill player (63%), including 22 rushes against the Patriots and 27 at Seattle a week later. He ran in three second-half TDs against the Seahawks, has already reached a career high of 10 TDs and is five away from setting the franchise's single-season record. Despite dealing with injuries of his own, Swift has not missed a game. — Courtney Cronin

4. Chicago Bears (4) They entered their bye as one of the league's hottest teams. Does it stay that way? There is nothing to think it won't.

What do you think of this week's rankings? The idle week didn't hurt them much, if at all.

#2598. Nets’ free-throw problem on full display in loss to 76ers

The Nets have been a bottom five team in the NBA this season from the free-throw line, and they certainly left too many points at the stripe in Monday's loss to the 76ers.

The Nets shot just 22-for-34 for a 64.7 percent conversion rate in their 12-point defeat. For the season, Brooklyn is ranked 26th in the league at 74.8 percent through its 3-10 start.

"Once again, I don't want to go to the players and be like, 'We gotta make free throws,' because then you go there and you're nervous," Nets coach Jordi Fernández said.

Jaylen Brown of the Philadelphia 76ers dribbles against Julius Randle of the Brooklyn Nets in New York, Monday, Nov. 16, 2026. The 76ers won 135-123. Getty Images

"Obviously I don't want to shoot 64 percent. … If we shoot better, we probably have a bigger chance. But I know our guys are good shooters and they're gonna make free throws. We gotta concentrate and make sure that we believe that all of them are going to go in."

Nolan Traore, Michael Porter Jr. and Julius Randle were a combined 19-for-21 from the line, but Egor Dëmin, Day'Ron Sharpe, Moritz Wagner and Danny Wolf combined to miss nine of 10 attempts.

Randle cut his lip in a face-to-face collision in Monday's fourth quarter with Philly's Jaylen Brown, who temporarily left the game to get his face bandaged. Brown also suffered a hamstring injury after returning to the floor.

"I'm fine. It feels terrible, to be honest. But I'm fine," Randle said. "I just went to trap him and he turned, and he didn't see me. Just kind of collided, but it's fine."

Julius Randle (30) of the Brooklyn Nets shoots a free throw against the Philadelphia 76ers in Brooklyn, N.Y., Monday, Nov. 16, 2026. NBAE via Getty Images

NBA legend Julius "Dr. J" Erving and former Nets coach Kevin Loughery will highlight the alumni present for a ceremony at halftime of Wednesday's game against the Bulls honoring the Nets' 1974 and 1976 ABA championship teams as part of the franchise's 60th season.

Others scheduled to attend include: Brian Taylor, Bill Melchionni, George Bucci, Jim Eakins, Rich Jones, Jim O'Brien, Billy Schaeffer, Al Skinner and Chuck Terry.

Nets rookie Mikel Brown Jr. launched a mentorship program called "Mikel's Crew" with a basketball clinic Tuesday with Brooklyn students from El Puente Beacon Leadership Center at MS 50 in Williamsburg.

"I feel like that's just what it's all about: influencing the youth and the community the right way," Brown said. "That's just how I grew up. I was influenced, I had a lot of mentors and people in my corner that kind of shaped me into who I am today."

The New York Yankees received a strong performance from their pitching staff in the opener of their American League Division Series matchup against the Tampa Bay Rays but had no answer for Drew Rasmussen. In order to avoid being pushed to the brink of elimination, they'll need to solve Freddy Peralta.

Make your MLB, Monday Night Football and NHL picks at BetMGM Sportsbook with promo code CBSSPORTS and get up to $1,500 in bonus bets if your first bet loses:

The Yankees look to even the ALDS when they visit Tropicana Field in St. Petersburg, Fla. on Monday to face the Rays in Game 2 at 8 p.m. ET. New York limited Tampa Bay to one run and five hits in Saturday's series opener but managed just one hit of its own in a 1-0 loss.

Jonathan Aranda belted a one-out solo homer off Gerrit Cole in the third inning and Rasmussen, who was making his second career postseason start and first since 2021, carried a no-hitter into the eighth. #2596. Buddy Kofoid’s Snowball Derby Run Proves He Wants NASCAR

Buddy Kofoid is one of the best dirt drivers in the world, yet he refuses to stop chasing his NASCAR dream. The 24-year-old from California has dominated sprint cars, but he wants to race on pavement just like Dale Earnhardt Jr. did.

Per Short Track Scene, Kofoid has been asking Toyota for chances to race on pavement every single year. He finally got his shot after the Knoxville Nationals when Trent Rodriguez told him they were running him in the Snowball Derby. Kofoid did not hesitate. "I have talked to (Toyota) every year trying to see if I can do a little bit more," Kofoid said of pavement racing. "It was after the Knoxville Nationals that (Trent Rodriguez) said, 'Hey, we are going to run you in the Derby,' and I was like, 'Okay, awesome,' and that was pretty much how it went."

Toyota is serious about seeing if Kofoid can make it to the Cup Series. Hendrick Motorsports is pondering further possibilities after Corey Day's recent triumph, as Christopher Bell strongly champions emerging talent. Funding was put together specifically to reward Kofoid's success and to take one more look at his NASCAR potential. Jack Irving, the Toyota Racing general manager, even asked Wilson Motorsports to pick out five or six races Kofoid could do.

Wilson Motorsports general manager Bond Suss explained the difficulty in finding time on the schedule. "But the hard part was there are no open weekends with the Sprint Car schedule," Suss said. The goal was to give Kofoid four races in a row to get acclimated, but the dirt schedule made that impossible. The Snowball Derby is the best chance they could find to get him on track without him driving a dirt car in between.

Kofoid knows that laps are the only way to learn a new surface. He told Suss that testing is a high priority and he will do as much as possible between his USAC Midget races out west. He is not afraid of the hard work that comes with learning a Super Late Model. "I told him this is a high priority and I will test as much as possible in between those races out west. The more laps the better in my book," he said.

The dirt community sometimes makes fun of how much pavement racers test, but Kofoid disagrees. "I agree with that 100 percent," Kofoid said. He knows that to win at Five Flags Speedway, he needs every bit of seat time he can get. He will test this week and next before the big race weekend.

Kofoid brings a strong resume to the event, including 17 victories this past season and back-to-back USAC National Midget championships. He will drive the No. 24 for Wilson Motorsports with support from Toyota and Mobil 1. From December 3-6 in Pensacola, Florida, FloRacing will stream his Snowball Derby debut for fans to view live.

#2593. Giants protect Henry Lalane, Marty Gair, and Josh Bostick from Rule 5 Draft; DFA Christian Koss and Rowan Wick

Rule 5 Draft protections had to be made on Tuesday afternoon, and the San Francisco Giants waited until the eleventh hour … well, beyond the eleventh hour. A full hour after the deadline passed, the Giants announced that they had protected a trio of players, all pitchers: right-handers Marty Gair and Josh Bostick, and left-hander Henry Lalane. To make space on the roster for that three, the Giants (who were operating with a 39-man roster after Sunday's Ryan Walker trade), designated for assignment infielder Christian Koss and right-handed reliever Rowan Wick.

Lalane was an obvious protection, and the lone slam dunk choice. Acquired from the New York Yankees in the Heliot Ramos trade, the 22-year old has fairly absurd physical tools. He quite literally stands out, as he's all of 6'7. He's still fairly raw, having spent most of the 2026 season in Low-A, where he accumulated a 2.74 ERA and a 2.63 FIP in 13 appearances, with 11.7 strikeouts per nine innings while working as a starter. He wasn't as sharp when he got promoted to High-A, but certainly held his own. The advanced metrics are extremely intriguing, and he ranks as the No. 11 prospect in the system per MLB Pipeline, so there really seemed to be no chance that the Giants would leave him unprotected.

Gair was a little bit more of a coin flip. Like Lalane, he was acquired at the deadline, as he came over with Ramon Marquez from the Philadelphia Phillies in exchange for Luis Arráez and Caleb Kilian. Gair is something of the classic Rule 5 protection debate: huge tools that require protecting, but raw enough to think you might be able to get away with not protecting (though that certainly didn't work in Spencer Miles' case a year ago). Gair, a pure reliever, has arguably the nastiest stuff in the system, and breezes past 100 mph. His absurd fastball/slider combo led to a truly comical 84 strikeouts in just 48 innings this year (33 innings in Low-A, 11 in High-A, and four in AA). He also walked 29 batters in those 48 innings, which is where the rawness comes into play, but you can see why the Giants were unwilling to risk losing his electric talents.

Bostick is the real surprise of the group. An eighth-round pick by the Giants in 2023, the just-turned 25-year old has been mighty impressive in his Minor League career. He has a four-pitch mix, and one of the better fastballs of any starting pitcher in the system. But, after spending all of 2025 in High-A (where he had a 3.71 ERA, a 4.59 FIP, and 10.5 strikeouts per nine innings), Bostick tore his Achilles in the weight room in the offseason, and lost the entirety of the 2026 season. Given his status as more of a good than great prospect, and the fact that no other teams have seen him pitch in the past year, or are aware of his health status, and I'm quite surprised that the Giants felt the need to protect him. He's certainly very talented, though, and could become a big part of the team's plans.

Perhaps more notable is the list of names the Giants didn't protect, which is highlighted by lefty Joe Whitman. The 2023 comp-round pick was one of the organization's top pitching prospects in 2026, when he had a 3.22 ERA, a 2.37 FIP, and 11.6 strikeouts per nine innings in AA, then a 3.74 ERA, a 4.73 FIP, and 7.4 strikeouts per nine in AAA. That's not a profile that, when attached to a lefty starter, you often see left unprotected. But the Giants tipped their hand a little bit when they called up Matt Wilkinson, Cesár Perdomo, and Yunior Marte (the latter straight from AA) at the end of the year, while leaving Whitman in AAA.

Extremely electric but extremely raw lefty Luis De La Torre was also left unprotected, along with righty relievers Tyler Vogel, Marques Johnson, and Will Bednar, switch-hitting AAA infielder Diego Velasquez, and recently-acquired reliever Blake Holub.

Just as noteworthy as the names of the players protected and not protected is that the Giants had to part ways with Koss. Most of the roster moves they had made to clear spots early in the offseason hadn't hurt, but this one does. Koss was not only hugely popular with the coaching staff, clubhouse, and fanbase, but had emerged as the play-anywhere backup infielder. With Shay Whitcomb, Osleivis Basabe, Brett Harris, and Nate Furman dumped earlier in the offseason, the Giants are now operating without a backup infielder on their roster, presuming Casey Schmitt opens the year in left field. It would seem that Schmitt and Marcelo Mayer will be counted on to fill in on the left side of the infield when Matt Chapman and Willy Adames need a day off.

Wick was DFA'd before ever pitching for the Giants. They signed him to a modest two-year deal last offseason, knowing he would miss the first year of the contract with an injury. Apparently they didn't like what they saw while he was rehabbing.

#2591. Should the Denver Broncos shake-up their starting offensive line?

One of the things that has been irritating many of us this season has been specific areas of offensive line play. I have seen people call out poor performances by Mike McGlinchey and Luke Wattenberg, but the real problem fans seem to see along the offensive line has been from interior guard Ben Powers.

Personally, I've seen him whiff on blocks and get turned around so frequently that I wonder if he is the primary reason Bo Nix has been quick to bail to his right as often as he does. It's not much better in the run game either, which is a source of constant frustration when watching these games.

Head Coach Sean Payton was asked about making changes to the offensive line and he seemed to downplay it a bit, but left the door open too.

"I made sure to make a point about evaluating all assets of what we're doing in our front in the offense," Payton said on Monday. "So I want to make sure one story doesn't lead to another. We'll spend an inordinate amount of time looking at mid-season cutups where we're at relative to scheme and personnel."

Frankly, I think they should make a change. If it gets a lot worse, then you can always change it back. I have nothing against Powers, but he has struggled and it is problematic for sustaining offensive drives. Making a change shouldn't be so hard to do. And maybe there are other things I don't see or cannot understand due to being on the outside looking in. If it's not Powers, then its someone in there not doing a good enough job and a change is certainly warranted.

What do you think: is Payton waiting too long to take action along the line?

Broncos quarterbacks past and present, how does Bo Nix measure up?

As Broncos fans, in our lifetime, we've had the absolute privilege of watching some of the best quarterbacks in football play for the Denver Broncos… and the frustration of having to watch the not-so-great struggle. Needless to say, Broncos fans know how to measure quarterback play, both good and bad, when they see it.

All of the Bo Nix clips from ManningCast on MNF in Week 10

Peyton and Eli Manning brought in Denver Broncos quarterback Bo Nix for a visit on ManningCast last night as the Los Angeles Chargers notched their first win of the season against the Baltimore Ravens.

NFL Power Rankings for Week 11: How did the Denver Broncos hold up over the bye?

The Denver Broncos didn't play last weekend, but a good chunk of prognosticators didn't move them an inch up or or down in their weekly power rankings.

On what changed with the anticipated trade for Chargers LB Daiyan Henley

"Nothing changed. It was already stated. Everything was pretty clearly spelled out. I'm not going to get into the specifics. He's a prospect we thought—and still do [think]—very highly of. It just didn't work out and it's not uncommon with trades. That's kind of where it went, and I'll leave it at that."

On his message to the team after the bye week and the areas of focus going forward

"I think collectively, we just finished a team meeting talking about the improvement in certain areas where we feel like we're going to have to be better at in this, call it, second half of the season. Specifically, I mentioned this last week, we need to block better on offense and we need to be in the right place. I thought we did an average job against Carolina, and I think that's an area of focus relative to more consistency in our run game. Then there were some third-down, fourth-down-and-longs defensively that was an Achilles heel for us a year ago, and the other day became one. Those are just a few things."

On if there is a loophole in the trade process

"I saw it all. There's no loophole. It just is part of the trade process every step of the way."

On the inside linebacker depth and if there are opportunities for more players to get snaps

"I don't view it the same way you do. We're going to play the starters and then guys that earn reps certainly will earn playing time. Yes, that's all I could say to that."

On the process for handling travel issues with the nationwide flight stoppage

"It's not that complex. [Vice President of Player Development] Ray [Jackson] does a good job of just finding out who's out of town, who may need assistance. I think he communicated several e-mails. Probably by yesterday, there were three players that were just finalizing their plans."

#2590. Predicting 2027 MLB Rookie of the Year candidates: Josue De Paula, Kade Anderson, Jesús Made and more

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

Tigers infielder Kevin McGonigle and Reds slugger Sal Stewart were named the 2026 Rookies of the Year on Monday night. McGonigle was the wire-to-wire leader for the award despite a stacked American League rookie class. In the National League, Stewart edged out Mets outfielder Carson Benge and Cardinals second baseman JJ Wetherholt, both of whom had excellent rookie campaigns.

No award gets you excited about the future the way Rookie of the Year does. It's a young player being recognized for his greatness, and great young players are what sports hopes are built on. With that in mind, here's a look ahead at the 2027 rookie class and, more importantly, who could be in the running for the 2027 Rookie of the Year awards.

Anderson made his debut in late August and gave the Mariners seven solid starts, though he remains rookie-eligible because he did not exceed the rookie limits of 50 innings or 45 days of service time. Anderson, the No. 3 pick in the 2025 Draft, is arguably the best pitching prospect in the game and is likely to have a rotation spot on Opening Day, which figures to boost his Rookie of the Year case. Add in a pitcher-friendly home ballpark, and Anderson is the super early favorite for the award. He had 167 strikeouts against only 22 walks in 129 innings between MLB and the minors in 2026.

One of the best prospects in the minors, Arias nearly made his MLB debut in September, but the Red Sox opted against it. He authored a .323/.400/.557 line with 25 home runs between Double-A and Triple-A in 2026, including a .331/.388/.506 line in 42 games at Triple-A as a 20-year-old. Trevor Story is entering the final year of his contract and has been healthy and productive at the same time once in the last four years. Arias likely gives Boston a better chance to win right now and I would not be surprised to see them turn the shortstop reins over to the youngster early next season. Early as in April.

Like Anderson, Jenkins made his MLB debut in late August, yet his rookie eligibility remains intact going into 2027. He had a rough go of it in the majors, slashing .226/.293/.393 in 26 games with the Twins, though his contact rates and plate discipline were impressive. Jenkins will turn only 22 in February and he is not the first top prospect to have a rough 26 games to begin his big-league career, nor will he be the last. There might be more growing pains to come next season, but Minnesota figures to give Jenkins a long runway to work through them. His 2027 could look like Benge's 2026, meaning sluggish early and sensational late.

It was only 11 games (plus four pinch-hitting appearances in the postseason), but gosh, De Paula was so impressive during his big-league debut. He's a precocious hitter with tremendous strike zone knowledge (13 walks and five strikeouts), and also some serious hard-hit ability. The biggest obstacle standing between De Paula and next year's Rookie of the Year award is playing time. Shohei Ohtani is locked in at DH and Andy Pages and Kyle Tucker aren't going anywhere. The Dodgers will have to either trade or bench Teoscar Hernández to get De Paula into the lineup. It would be worth it. The Yordan Alvarez comps De Paula got in the minors don't seem so insane now.

The Brewers are the World Series champions and they also have arguably the best farm system in the game with the consensus No. 1 prospect in Made. Still only 19, Made performed admirably in a full season at Double-A this year, and he's currently playing very well against grown men in the Dominican Winter League. He figures to open next season in Triple-A, with a May or June promotion to Milwaukee in the cards. That could put Made at a disadvantage in the Rookie of the Year race. Either way, it's only a matter of time until the defending champions add the game's best prospect to their lineup, presumably at third base.

At 20 years and 121 days, Salas became the youngest catcher to ever appear in a postseason game in Game 2 of this year's Wild Card Series. He started three of San Diego's six postseason games after making his MLB debut in September, and it seems likely Salas will take over as their starting backstop next season. I think he's a longshot Rookie of the Year candidate simply because it's really hard to be a rookie catcher, and next year Salas will be the youngest regular catcher since Hall of Famer Ivan Rodriguez in 1991. Still, Salas is a special defender with promising offensive chops.

Several prominent Japanese veterans will make their way to MLB via the posting system this offseason. We don't know where they will sign yet, but the rules say these players will be Rookie of the Year-eligible regardless of their age or years of experience in Japan, so we're going to include them here.

We ranked Sato as the best position player free agent on the market this offseason. Japan's reigning Triple Crown winner has tremendous left-handed power. We're talking legitimate 30-homer upside. Sato does swing and miss a bunch, though, and he's an aggressive hitter who's unlikely to walk as much as Munetaka Murakami, which could hold him back at the plate. Add in questionable defense at the hot corner and it's unclear exactly how much impact Sato will have in the big leagues. Bottom line though, guys with 30-homer power will always be in the Rookie of the Year conversation.

Taira, our No. 19 free agent, is destined to be a fan favorite given his fire hydrant build (5-foot-8 and 220 lbs.) and bat-missing fastball. He gets close to seven feet of extension down the mound despite his height, creating a unique release window and an "upshoot" effect on his fastball. Taira started for the Seibu Lions in 2026 after spending 2024 and 2025 in the bullpen. I assume the team that signs him will give him a chance to start next year. If he winds up in relief, Taira has the stuff and gumption to get high-leverage outs in the late innings.

#2589. NHL Power Rankings: Flyers flounder to start new season as Rick Tocchet searches for answers

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

I hate to get so negative just one week into the season, but the Philadelphia Flyers have forced my hand. After a magical run to the second round of the 2026 Stanley Cup Playoffs, the Flyers have fallen on their face through four games.

Philadelphia opened the season with a 7-0 loss to the rival Pittsburgh Penguins, and coach Rick Tocchet described his team's play as "disturbing." There was only one way for the season to go after that, right? Wrong.

The Flyers are off to an 0-2-2 start, and the underlying numbers aren't pretty. Per Natural Stat Trick, they have a five-on-five expected goals share of 26.0%, which ranks last in the NHL. Their 4.57 xGA/60 also ranks last. Their 1.94 xGF/60? You guessed it. Last.

Tocchet's bunch entered the season with a lot of well-earned optimism. Even with subpar play from Matvei Michkov last season, the Flyers managed to reach the Eastern Conference Semifinals. Rookie Porter Martone asserted himself as a budding star with six goals and nine assists in 19 games between the regular season and playoffs.

There's still plenty of time -- 80 games exactly -- for the Flyers to get back on track and restore that optimism, but to say this has been a discouraging start would be an understatement.

#2586. 2026 MLB Rookie of the Year: Tigers' Kevin McGonigle, Reds' Sal Stewart win BBWAA awards

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

Kevin McGonigle of the Tigers and Sal Stewart of the Reds were named the 2026 Rookies of the Year in their respective leagues on Monday night as part of the BBWAA's awards week. McGonigle earned 28 of 30 first-place votes, beating out the Guardians' Parker Messick and the Red Sox's Payton Tolle. Stewart, meanwhile, beat the Mets' Carson Benge and the Cardinals' JJ Wetherholt.

Because McGonigle and Stewart were both with the major-league team for long enough to earn a full year of service time, the Tigers and Reds will each receive a Prospect Promotion Incentive pick in the 2027 MLB Draft.

The annual awards, which also include Manager of the Year, Reliever of the Year, Cy Young and MVP, are voted on by 30 members of the Baseball Writers Association of America (that's two per MLB city in each league). Votes were submitted before the beginning of the playoffs, meaning that only regular-season contributions are taken into account.

Stewart won the battle of Old School stats vs. New School stats here. Though he only posted 2.0 WAR, he had 32 home runs and 111 RBI, putting him in rarefied air for a rookie. He's one of just 15 rookies ever with at least 30 homers and 100 RBI. The only names from that list to not win the award either faced another player from the list or played before Rookie of the Year was awarded. Everyone else has taken home the hardware, just as Stewart did Monday evening.

Overall, Stewart appeared in all 162 games, hitting .263/.330/.457 (117 OPS+) with 25 doubles, 32 homers, 112 RBI, 87 runs and 15 steals.

Stewart earned 20 of the 30 available first-place votes.

Carson Benge of the Mets finished second and JJ Wetherholt of the Cardinals finished in third place. Benge, the 2024 first-rounder, made the team out of spring training and hit .282/.346/.430 with 20 home runs, 22 steals and 4.3 WAR. Defensive metrics love Wetherholt and helped push him to 4.5 WAR in 139 games. He hit .242/.339/.365 with 17 homers, 14 steals and 89 runs.

Stewart joins the following Reds as Rookie of the Year winners:

The honor for McGonigle completes a stellar year for the former first-round draft pick. He broke camp with the Tigers and was productive from the get-go. He ended up hitting .278/.376/.430 (126 OPS+) with 28 doubles, five triples, 18 home runs, 72 RBI, 97 runs, 12 steals and 7.1 WAR, the latter good enough for the AL lead among position players. He played great defense, ran the bases well and was an All-Star. He nearly walked (95) as much as he struck out (100), too. Not much more could've been asked of the Pennsylvania native who played most of the season at age 21, and he's a well-deserving Rookie of the Year.

A few weeks after he debuted, he and the team agreed to an eight-year, $150 million extension.

McGonigle won in a blowout, getting 28 of the 30 available first-place votes, scoring 204 of a possible 210 points.

He joins the following players who have won the award with the Tigers:

Parker Messick of the Guardians finishes second after going 12-9 with a 2.56 ERA, 1.06 WHIP and 193 strikeouts in 186 ⅓ innings; he is also a top-three finalist for the Cy Young award. Red Sox starter Payton Tolle finishes third after going 9-6 with a 3.03 ERA (135 ERA+), 1.10 WHIP and 171 strikeouts in 148 ⅔ innings.

#2585. Chiefs sign former Eagles offensive lineman to practice squad

On Tuesday, the Kansas City Chiefs hosted five players at the team facility for a tryout, according to the NFL Transactions Report.

The team also reportedly had former Philadelphia Eagles offensive lineman Fred Johnson at its facility, according to Jason Anderson of 810 Sports.

The NFL's daily report shows that the Chiefs signed tight end John FitzPatrick to the practice squad of the tryout group. E.J. Smith was also brought back to the reserve unit.

However, later in the evening, the Chiefs' website also listed Johnson as a third practice squad signing.

Johnson is an eight-year veteran who started his career with the Cincinnati Bengals as an undrafted free agent out of Florida in 2019. He started eight games over three years, but the most time he has seen on the field has been the last four years with the Eagles.

Johnson started in 14 regular-season games in 2024 and 2025; he also played in all four playoff games through beating Kansas City in the Super Bowl. He primarily lined up at right tackle (726 snaps) during that time, but he also played 419 snaps at left tackle.

Earlier in his NFL career, Johnson spent a stretch of time at right guard.

Among the other names the Chiefs tried out, the most notable is Prater, a two-time Pro Bowl kicker who last kicked for the Buffalo Bills at age 41 last year. He made 18 of 20 field goal attempts, missing one of his two attempts from over 50 yards and another from short range. He also missed three point-after attempts.

It's also notable that three defensive tackles were brought in. Graves most recently spent time on the Houston Texans' practice squad after a college career at the University of Iowa. Singleton spent last year on the Seattle Seahawks' practice squad and was waived after this preseason.

But Eric Johnson — the former Missouri State Bear — is a four-year NFL veteran with 41 tackles, two tackles for loss and one sack in his career with the Indianapolis Colts and New England Patriots. He hasn't played since 2025 after spending time on multiple teams practice squads over the last year.

Second-year defensive tackle Omarr Norman-Lott's (knee) status this week will be worth monitoring.

#2582. Bob Boone, All-Star catcher, 1980 World Series champion and father of Yankees manager, dies at 78

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

Bob Boone, a four-time All-Star catcher and the middle member of a three-generation baseball family, has died. He was 78. His son, Bret Boone, made the announcement on Tuesday. No cause of death was given.

My dad- He was my mentor, my coach, my rock. He taught me how to be a pro and more importantly, how to be a man. He was one of the highest integrity people I’ve ever known and I’m going to miss him dearly. Baseball lost a great one yesterday. R.I.P dad, I love you❤️ pic.twitter.com/4NtYAwXIv3

"Bob Boone had an enduring impact on the field as a 19-year MLB veteran, a seven-time Gold Glove Award-winning catcher, a four-time All-Star and 1980 World Champion with the Philadelphia Phillies," the MLB Players Association said in a statement. "He embraced a leadership role in the Players Association early in his career, and earned a reputation as a strong and principled voice in the advancement of player rights in the 1970s and '80s ... As we honor Bob's legacy and mourn his passing, we extend our heartfelt condolences to his wife, Sue, sons Aaron, Bret and Matt, his extended family, and his many fans and admirers throughout the game."

The Boones were baseball's first three-generation family. Bob's father, Ray Boone, played for six teams from 1948-60, and his sons Aaron and Bret both had long careers spanning the 1990s and 2000s. Bob's other son, Matt, played in the minor leagues.

"I'm just so grateful that I had a dad that took us to work with him all the time," Aaron, now manager of the New York Yankees, said in 2023 (via MLB.com). "He came up at the end of '72, and I was born in the spring of '73. He played until my senior year in high school and literally I was at the ballpark -- my brothers and I, in unis, shagging (fly balls) and doing everything you could possibly imagine. It was a great way to grow up."

Born in San Diego, Bob Boone made his MLB debut with the Phillies in 1972 and took over as the club's starting catcher in 1973. He hit 10 home runs and finished third in the National League Rookie of the Year voting. That started a 17-year run as one of the game's best and most durable catchers. Boone started at least 130 games behind the plate eight times in his career and 110 games 14 times.

With the Phillies in 1980, Boone went 7 for 17 (.412) with four walks and zero strikeouts in Philadelphia's six-game World Series win over the Kansas City Royals.

A seven-time Gold Glove winner, including four straight during his age-38 to -41 seasons, Boone had his most productive years with the Phillies from 1976-79. He hit .282/.351/.414 those four seasons and averaged nine home runs, which was excellent output given the offensive standard at the catcher position during that era. Boone went to four All-Star Games and received MVP votes twice.

"Bob was an incredible player, teammate and family man," the Phillies said in a statement. "He embodied everything we believe exemplary athletes should represent, both on and off the field. We were proud to have him as part of the Phillies family during one of the most historic runs in team history. His impact on our organization, his teammates, and everyone who had the privilege of knowing him will never be forgotten."

Boone ranks second with 2,161 games at catcher during the Modern Era (since 1900), behind only Hall of Famer Ivan Rodriguez (2,377). He is 15th among primary catchers with 1,838 hits and 21st with 2,508 total bases. Boone played parts of 19 big league seasons with the Phillies (1972-81), California Angels (1982-88), and Royals (1989-90).

The Orlando SunRays, a potential expansion franchise, hired Boone to be their manager soon after he retired as a player, though the expansion franchises were instead awarded to Denver and Miami in 1991. Boone later managed the Royals from 1995-97 and the Cincinnati Reds (2001-03). He managed his son, Aaron, those years with the Reds.

In 2005, Boone joined the Washington Nationals as their director of player development and had a hand in building the core that won the franchise's first World Series title in 2019. He remained with the Nationals until 2021. Boone spent five years on the Hall of Fame ballot from 1996 to 2000 but was not voted into Cooperstown.

#2578. Drake Maye injury update: Patriots reportedly fear QB fractured ankle, could miss rest of season

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

The New England Patriots may have to finish the 2026 season without their franchise centerpiece. Quarterback Drake Maye is believed to have suffered a significant lower-leg injury that is poised to sideline him for an extended period of time, according ESPN. The report notes that the injury has the potential to keep Maye out for the remainder of the year. Specifically, ESPN reports that the team fears Maye fractured his ankle.

Maye suffered the injury on the final offensive snap of New England's opening drive against the Detroit Lions during their Week 10 matchup in Munich, Germany. The third-year quarterback was sacked by pass rusher Aidan Hutchinson on a third-and-goal play and was in noticeable discomfort after the hit. After being looked at on the sideline, Maye gingerly walked to the locker room where he was eventually ruled out with what the team called an ankle injury.

Immediately after the game, coach Mike Vrabel didn't have much of an update on Maye's status. However, Vrabel told WEEI's "The Greg Hill Show" on Monday morning that Maye stayed back in Germany.

"The update that I have is just out of caution, Drake stayed back,' Vrabel said, via the Boston Herald. "He'll be traveling back here shortly. But just wanted to make sure that everything was good for him to travel back and safely. The things that go around injuries, and just wanted to make sure everything was in line for him to travel, and it seems like he is. He'll be returning here, I think, shortly."

Given that Maye was unable to travel back with the team following the international contest, this lends credence to this latest report on the severity of the injury. ESPN's report highlights that Maye stayed in Germany to undergo additional tests to determine whether he needs surgery.

Maye -- along with the entire Patriots team -- has come back down to earth a bit in 2026 following his MVP runner-up season last year as New England made a surprise Super Bowl run. Through 10 games, Maye was 5-5 as the starter, completed 65.6% of his passes, averaged 233.0 passing yards per game, and threw for 18 touchdowns. He's also thrown 11 interceptions, which are already a career high.

Of course, it's never a good time for your franchise quarterback to endure a potential season-ending injury, but Maye going down comes at a critical juncture of New England's season. The club is reeling after losing three of its last four games, dropping it back to .500 on the season.

This latest loss to Detroit pushes them further behind the Buffalo Bills (8-1) in the AFC East race, and they are now on the outside looking in on the AFC playoff picture. Coming into Week 10, they were slotted as the No. 7 seed, but are now sitting as the No. 8 seed and looking up to the Cleveland Browns (6-4), Pittsburgh Steelers (6-3), and Denver Broncos (7-2) for the three wild card spots.

The Patriots will have the bye to collect themselves in Week 11, but the road ahead doesn't get any easier, particularly in December, when they'll face the Bills, Vikings, and Chiefs (road) over a three-week span. Not having Maye for those matchups would make New England significant underdogs, even with two of those games at Gillette Stadium.

With Maye on the shelf, the Patriots will first turn to top backup Tommy DeVito. He stepped in during their contest with Detroit in Germany on Sunday. In that game, DeVito put up less-than-stellar numbers, completing 12-of-24 for 81 yards, a touchdown and an interception. He also rushed four times for 19 yards on the ground.

DeVito has been with New England for the past two seasons after being claimed off waivers in August of 2025 following his release from the New York Giants. Last offseason, he signed a two-year, $7.4 million extension with the team and became the primary back to Maye entering 2026.

The 28-year-old has starting experience, having logged eight starts over his career since entering the NFL in 2023 as an undrafted free agent out of Illinois. DeVito is 3-5 over those starts and has a 63.4% completion percentage to go along with an 84.6 passer rating for his career.
